api/LastFleet.AI.Barks.BarkKind.html.summary: Enum BarkKind Namespace LastFleet.AI.Barks Assembly LastFleet.AI.dll What a soldier calls out. Every bark is triggered by a real decision or event, never by a timer, so listening to the squad tells the player what it's about to do. public enum BarkKind : byte Fields None = 0 No bark (the default). Contact = 1 Spotted an enemy. LostContact = 2 The enemy broke line of sight, and the soldier is heading to where he was. Searching = 3 Reached the last known position and found nothing. StandDown = 4 Gave up the search. FlankingLeft = 5 Took the flanker role and is moving around the enemy's left (from the squad's point of view). FlankingRight = 6 Took the flanker role and is moving around the enemy's right. CoveringFire = 7 The suppressor opened covering fire. MovingUp = 8 Decided to advance to closer cover. Pushing = 9 Decided to rush the enemy. TargetReloading = 10 Saw the enemy reloading, and is pushing because of it. FallingBack = 11 Decided to fall back to farther cover, or the squad is retreating. Reloading = 12 Started reloading during a fight. FragOut = 13 Threw a grenade. GrenadeWarning = 14 An enemy grenade landed close, and the soldier is running from it. ManDown = 15 A squadmate died. Pinned = 16 Near misses have the soldier pinned down. Choir = 17 Spotted the Choir (the horde, or its soldiers).

api/LastFleet.AI.Behavior.BehaviorAction.title: Enum BehaviorAction | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.AI.Behavior.BehaviorAction.summary: Enum BehaviorAction Namespace LastFleet.AI.Behavior Assembly LastFleet.AI.dll The actions a soldier can perform, each one a leaf of its behavior tree. The game decides how each is done (the soldier's movement, aim and tactics); the tree decides when. public enum BehaviorAction : byte Fields Roam = 0 Walk its patrol route, or look around where it's standing. Always succeeds. WatchEnemy = 1 Turn to face where the enemy was noticed while it reacts. Always succeeds. ChooseIntent = 2 Score hold, advance, push and fall back (using the behavior's scoring) and take the best one as its intent. Always succeeds. FightFromCover = 3 Fight from cover according to its intent: hold, move up, fall back or push, all in one action. Always succeeds. The shipped tree uses HoldCover, BoundForward, PushEnemy and FallBack instead, so each one shows up separately. FightInOpen = 4 Fight in the open: aim, fire in bursts, stay in its range band, strafe. Always succeeds. ClearRooms = 5 Clear the rooms between it and the enemy together with its squad, stacking up at doors. Fails if there are no rooms to clear. GoToEnemy = 6 Go to the enemy's last known position. Always succeeds. LookAround = 7 Stand still and look around for the enemy. Always succeeds. TopUpMagazine = 8 Reload when there's nobody to shoot and the magazine is low. Always succeeds. ThrowGrenade = 9 Throw a grenade where the enemy is hiding, if the squad is allowed to and the throw is clear. Always succeeds. DodgeGrenades = 10 Run from grenades landing nearby. Always succeeds. HoldCover = 11 Stay in its cover (or take the best one nearby), peek out and fire, and duck when hit. A flanker takes cover around the side. Always succeeds (it fights in the open if there's no cover). BoundForward = 12 Bound forward with the squad. The soldier farthest back moves first, to cover near or in front of the squad's lead, while the rest cover it, and nobody gets farther ahead than the squad's cohesion allows. Succeeds while it bounds (or holds the cover it bounded to). Fails if it isn't its turn or there's no cover ahead to bound to. PushEnemy = 13 Leave cover and close in on the enemy, firing. Always succeeds. FallBack = 14 Fall back to cover farther from the enemy, one bound at a time. Always succeeds. SearchForEnemy = 15 Search for a lost enemy where he most likely went: past the doorways he was heading for (out to the node's value in rooms, 2 if not set), straight ahead along his path, and where he was last seen. The squad splits the guesses up and each soldier checks the most likely one near it. Fails once every guess has been checked.

api/LastFleet.AI.Behavior.BehaviorNodeKi.title: Enum BehaviorNodeKind | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.AI.Behavior.BehaviorNodeKi.summary: Enum BehaviorNodeKind Namespace LastFleet.AI.Behavior Assembly LastFleet.AI.dll The type of a node in a soldier's behavior tree: how it decides whether it succeeds, and what it does. public enum BehaviorNodeKind : byte Fields Selector = 0 Tries its children in order and succeeds on the first one that succeeds. Fails if none do. Sequence = 1 Runs its children in order as long as they succeed. Fails at the first one that fails. All = 2 Runs every child regardless of result, then succeeds. Used for things done every update alongside the main choice. Not = 3 Succeeds when its single child fails, and fails when it succeeds. Awareness = 4 Succeeds while the soldier's awareness matches the one named (idle, alerted, engaging, hunting, searching). Check = 5 Succeeds while one of the combat scoring inputs passes the given comparison (for example range > 20). HasCover = 6 Succeeds if the level has cover points to fight from. SquadAlive = 7 Succeeds while the number of squad members still standing passes the given comparison. DistanceToEnemy = 8 Succeeds while the distance to the enemy's last known position passes the given comparison, in meters. SeesEnemy = 9 Succeeds while the soldier can see an enemy. Intent = 10 Succeeds while the soldier's intent matches the one named (hold, advance, push, fall back). Action = 11 Runs one of the soldier's actions (BehaviorAction).

api/LastFleet.AI.Behavior.BodyAbility.ht.title: Enum BodyAbility | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.AI.Behavior.BodyAbility.ht.summary: Enum BodyAbility Namespace LastFleet.AI.Behavior Assembly LastFleet.AI.dll Something a soldier's body has to be able to animate for its behavior to work. Behaviors never name animations, but a behavior that throws grenades needs a body that can visibly throw. public enum BodyAbility : byte Fields Fire = 0 Fires its gun, with the shot's recoil (the graph's fire action). Reload = 1 Swaps its gun's magazine (the graph's reload action). Throw = 2 Throws a grenade (the graph's throw action). Crouch = 3 Crouches, behind low cover or in the open. Lean = 4 Leans out around cover to fire, then back in. BlindFire = 5 Fires blind over or around cover, with the gun up and the head down. Remarks A body type's animation graph (content/anim) lists what it supports under capabilities. A behavior's needs come from the actions in its tree (Needs). If an enemy variant's behavior needs something its body can't animate, that's reported as a problem when the data is loaded. In the data, each value is written the way Name(BodyAbility) returns it (for example blindFire).

api/LastFleet.AI.Director.DirectorSystem.title: Class DirectorSystem | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.AI.Director.DirectorSystem.summary: Class DirectorSystem Namespace LastFleet.AI.Director Assembly LastFleet.AI.dll The Director (design doc, "AI director"). It reads how much pressure the squad is under and paces the fight around that, like Left 4 Dead's director. public sealed class DirectorSystem : ISimulationSystem Inheritance object DirectorSystem Implements ISimulationSystem Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Each player's Stress goes up when they take damage or get downed, and fades once they're safe. The squad's stress is that of the most stressed player still standing. During build-up, a squad left alone too long gets a patrol from the nearest spawn closet (never one in view, near anyone, or behind a gate it hasn't opened), sized for the number of players. At a peak, nothing new gets sent. While relaxing, the hack's waves are delayed a little (HoldWaves). On top of that, the station's alert (Alert) rises with time on the level and with noise, and barely drops. The higher the alert, the sooner, bigger and more numerous the patrols (AlertTuning). Like in Alien: Isolation, the Director knows where the squad is but its soldiers don't: it sends them to look nearby, sweeping room to room, and pulls them back if they crowd the squad too long without a fight (Hunt(ref DirectorState, float, bool, float)). Runs with the command systems, after the MissionSystem, whose closets it uses. Only a mission level has a DirectorState (Spawn(GameWorld)); without one this does nothing. Deterministic, and doesn't allocate except on ticks where it adds a player's stress component or sends a patrol. Constructors DirectorSystem(MissionSystem, DirectorTuning?) The Director (design doc, "AI director"). It reads how much pressure the squad is under and paces the fight around that, like Left 4 Dead's director. public DirectorSystem(MissionSystem mission, DirectorTuning? tuning = null) Parameters mission MissionSystem tuning DirectorTuning Remarks Each player's Stress goes up when they take damage or get downed, and fades once they're safe. The squad's stress is that of the most stressed player still standing. During build-up, a squad left alone too long gets a patrol from the nearest spawn closet (never one in view, near anyone, or behind a gate it hasn't opened), sized for the number of players. At a peak, nothing new gets sent. While relaxing, the hack's waves are delayed a little (HoldWaves). On top of that, the station's alert (Alert) rises with time on the level and with noise, and barely drops. The higher the alert, the sooner, bigger and more numerous the patrols (AlertTuning). Like in Alien: Isolation, the Director knows where the squad is but its soldiers don't: it sends them to look nearby, sweeping room to room, and pulls them back if they crowd the squad too long without a fight (Hunt(ref DirectorState, float, bool, float)). Runs with the command systems, after the MissionSystem, whose closets it uses. Only a mission level has a DirectorState (Spawn(GameWorld)); without one this does nothing. Deterministic, and doesn't allocate except on ticks where it adds a player's stress component or sends a patrol. A mission at the sector's gate takes the fleet through into the next sector. api/LastFleet.AI.Fleet.SystemKnowledge.h.summary: Enum SystemKnowledge Namespace LastFleet.AI.Fleet Assembly LastFleet.AI.dll What the fleet knows of a star system (design doc, "Knowledge states"). The map shows each differently: what can't be seen is the point. public enum SystemKnowledge Fields Unknown = 0 Nothing: a faint star, no name, no lanes. Charted = 1 Charted: its lanes and name, from the fleet's charts (two jumps out), but not what's there. api/LastFleet.AI.Fleet.html.title: Namespace LastFleet.AI.Fleet | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.AI.Fleet.html.summary: Namespace LastFleet.AI.Fleet Classes CampaignTarget Something the fleet can raid in a star system (content/defs/campaign.json): a station, or a ship of one of the plans. CampaignTuning What the fleet finds to raid as it crosses the sectors (content/defs/campaign.json): stations, laid out by the station plans, and ships (frigates, carriers, strike carriers), each laid out by its plan, each turning up as often as its weight once the fleet has come far enough. Each system has a few of them (its points of interest), and a sector's first system and its gate always have a station first. A point raided is picked over: its cargo thinner, its guards heavier. FleetNeed One line on the needs board: a supply, how many jumps the fleet's stock of it will last, and the text shown. FleetShip One ship in the fleet: its kind, its name, how many people are aboard, and its condition (0 is lost, 100 is undamaged). FleetSim The fleet's simulation between missions (design doc, "The Fleet: home base" and "The Scourge at the strategic layer"). FleetState The fleet's state between missions (design doc, "The Fleet: home base"): its ships and people, its stock of each supply, its morale, how many missions and jumps it has made, and how far behind the Scourge is. FleetVote The squad's votes at the star map (design doc, "Co-op design": voting at the star map). Everyone picks a course, and the course is the one most of them picked. Everyone can vote to jump, and the fleet jumps once more than half the squad has. The host breaks ties: a course they picked wins a tie, and their vote to jump carries a split squad. Galaxy The galaxy the fleet is running across (design doc, "Vast to look at, few choices to make"): a seeded spiral of stars, with every sector a region of it. The fleet starts near the core and runs outward along an arm, a sector at a time, so its trail leads back across everything it's crossed. JumpTuning How the fleet's jump plays out on the ship (campaign.json's jump): the countdown once the squad has voted, how far the lights go down while the drive spools up, and the flash and shake as it jumps. LockerItem A weapon or a loose part in the armory's locker (design doc, "The armoury"). The locker is the fleet's, so it's everyone's: kept between missions, and anyone on the ship can take from it or put into it. PointOfInterest Somewhere in a star system the squad can drop to (design doc, "Jumping and points of interest"): a station, or a ship of one of the plans. Holds its seed and the settings it's generated with: how heavily it's guarded and what its cargo is mostly made of. StarMap Builds and queries the sector the fleet is crossing (design doc, "Map structure"). A sector has ten to fourteen systems from its entry (on the left) to its gate (on the right). Each is linked to its nearest neighbors so there are alternate routes, and each has a few points of interest to drop to, stations and ships. StarSystem A star system in the sector the fleet is crossing (design doc, "Star map"). Holds its map position, its lanes, and its points of interest: the stations and ships there the squad can drop to. Structs GalaxyStar One star of the galaxy behind the sectors, as the map draws it. Enums ShipKind A fleet ship's role (design doc, "Ships and modules"). SystemKnowledge What the fleet knows of a star system (design doc, "Knowledge states"). The map shows each differently: what can't be seen is the point.

api/LastFleet.AI.Horde.HordeField.html.summary: Class HordeField Namespace LastFleet.AI.Horde Assembly LastFleet.AI.dll One flow field for the whole horde (design doc, "Horde simulation"). Instead of a path per swarmling, every spot in the level knows which direction leads to the nearest player. public sealed class HordeField Inheritance object HordeField Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks It works on two levels, like the soldiers' NavClusters. A search over clusters (each 4 m square of each floor) outward from the players gives every cluster the next cluster toward them. Inside a cluster, a small field, built the first time it's needed and then cached, gives each cell the step toward that next cluster. So hundreds of swarmlings cost one lookup each. The grid is built with the mission's doors open, and here the floor in each doorway is its own cluster. A shut door (SetDoor(int, bool)) closes its cluster, so the field routes around it (or nowhere) and nobody walks through. Deterministic, since the cached fields only depend on the grid. Not thread-safe. Constructors HordeField(NavGrid, IReadOnlyList<(Vector3 Center, Vector3 HalfExtents)>?) That's a room's shut door, which opens for whoever comes or which the swarm batters open. public void SetBarred(int door, bool barred) Parameters door int barred bool SetDoor(int, bool) Shuts or opens a doorway (indexed in the order given when the field was built). public void SetDoor(int door, bool shut) Parameters door int shut bool TryStep(int, out int, out int) Gets the next step from cell toward the nearest goal: either a direction to walk (0 to 7, as in Direction(int)) or a ledge to drop off (landing). Not characters: no controller, no physics body, no brain. Each runs over the navigation grid down one shared HordeField towards the nearest player, straight at them once close and in the open, keeps apart from the others by a spatial hash, and lunges: a short wind-up (the telegraph) and a bite. Shots and grenades kill them (the shot and grenade systems test Swarmling bodies) and knock them back; the dead lie a moment and are gone. public sealed class HordeSystem : ISimulationSystem Inheritance object HordeSystem Implements ISimulationSystem Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Hordes come when the mission calls for them: now and then while the squad infiltrates and the Director is building up, with every wave of the hack, and when the extraction starts, with a trickle in between those two. They come out of the floor where the players are not looking, 25 to 55 m away by the way there; or through the station's hull breaches (Breach): a fresh horde may blow one open, 18 to 55 m away by the way and with nobody right by it (in a blast of debris and smoke), and pour in through it, dropping out of the hole into the room; once open, a breach is a way in for every horde after. Call(int) sends one at any time (the developer tools, --horde). One of the world's late systems (SimulationSetup.CreateWorld's lateSystems): it moves after the characters and logs its bites as hits. Deterministic; allocation-free on most ticks. Constructors HordeSystem(ICollisionWorld, NavGrid, HitLog, ulong, HordeTuning?, DestructionLog?) api/LastFleet.AI.Horde.html.title: Namespace LastFleet.AI.Horde | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.AI.Horde.html.summary: Namespace LastFleet.AI.Horde Classes HordeField One flow field for the whole horde (design doc, "Horde simulation"). Instead of a path per swarmling, every spot in the level knows which direction leads to the nearest player. HordeSystem The horde (design doc, "Horde simulation"): the Choir's swarmlings, hundreds at once. Not characters: no controller, no physics body, no brain. Each runs over the navigation grid down one shared HordeField towards the nearest player, straight at them once close and in the open, keeps apart from the others by a spatial hash, and lunges: a short wind-up (the telegraph) and a bite. Shots and grenades kill them (the shot and grenade systems test Swarmling bodies) and knock them back; the dead lie a moment and are gone. HordeTuning How the horde moves, attacks and spawns (design doc, "Horde simulation"). Times are in seconds, lengths in meters.

api/LastFleet.AI.Missions.MissionSystem..summary: Class MissionSystem Namespace LastFleet.AI.Missions Assembly LastFleet.AI.dll A boarding action (design doc, "Boarding action: a ship in the fight"): the warship the squad is on is in a fight with the fleet. The fleet's guns hit it on a cadence (each hit counted in HitCount, so everyone aboard feels it); a hit hurts those near it, and sometimes starts a fire or blows a window. Fires spread room to room and burn out, unless the ship's fire suppression is running: its sprinklers put them out, until a hit knocks it out (repaired at its controls in damage control) or its power goes (cutting the reactor kills it). While its batteries fire, the fleet takes damage. The squad silences the batteries and cuts the reactor by holding Interact at each, then takes the bridge; a battery or the reactor lost with its room to a breach is out for good. public sealed class MissionSystem : ISimulationSystem Inheritance object MissionSystem Implements ISimulationSystem Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Keycards are taken by walking over them, by anyone standing (not downed); the squad shares them. A locked door opens when someone standing comes near it with its keycard held. Holding Interact at the terminal starts the hack, which runs while anyone standing is in the terminal's room and pauses while nobody is. Once the hack is done, the mission succeeds when everyone still alive is standing at the extraction point together for a moment. It fails when nobody is standing: everyone down or dead at once (alone, dying is enough). Reinforcement waves grow with the number of players. A wave's soldiers wait as Pending until a spawn closet can take them: one by the arena or extraction first, nearest the terminal, whose door is shut, with nobody inside and nobody standing within SpawnClearance. They appear inside, out of sight, its door opens, they hunt towards the terminal, and the door shuts once the closet is empty again. A level without closets uses its fallback points, but never one anyone can see or is near. Runs with the command systems, after the soldiers' AI, so this tick's commands (Interact) are read as given. The mission's state is one MissionState entity; keycards are MissionKey entities, locks MissionLock and closet doors ClosetDoor entities. Spawn(GameWorld, MissionPlan) creates them and Restart(GameWorld) renews them. Doors through bulkheads are SealableDoor entities (gates' beside their locks), shut while Seal(int) has their compartment sealed. A world without them (the range, the outpost) has no mission, and this system does nothing. Allocation-free except on the ticks soldiers spawn. api/LastFleet.AI.Missions.TankPumpSystem.summary: Class TankPumpSystem Namespace LastFleet.AI.Missions Assembly LastFleet.AI.dll Pumps supply tanks (SupplyTank) into the docked dropship. Whatever gets pumped belongs to the fleet immediately (Delivered), even if the mission fails afterward. public sealed class TankPumpSystem : ISimulationSystem Inheritance object TankPumpSystem Implements ISimulationSystem Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks The station hears the pumping. Once a tank starts, the Director sends a patrol for it out of the nearest closet, plus a horde if the mission's hordes are active. An enemy standing on the hose for CutSeconds cuts it, and pumping stops until a player repairs it. When the hack starts the dropship undocks, and any tank that isn't empty yet stays as it is. Once all the valves on a deep reservoir's pipe are open, the station hears the pipe fill and sends a patrol to the reservoir. This is one of the command systems and runs after the mission system (it reads and adds to the mission state). Dragging and connecting the hoses is done by the simulation (TankSystem). Doesn't allocate. Constructors TankPumpSystem(MissionSystem, HordeSystem?) Pumps supply tanks (SupplyTank) into the docked dropship. Whatever gets pumped belongs to the fleet immediately (Delivered), even if the mission fails afterward. public TankPumpSystem(MissionSystem mission, HordeSystem? horde = null) Parameters mission MissionSystem horde HordeSystem Remarks The station hears the pumping. Once a tank starts, the Director sends a patrol for it out of the nearest closet, plus a horde if the mission's hordes are active. An enemy standing on the hose for CutSeconds cuts it, and pumping stops until a player repairs it. When the hack starts the dropship undocks, and any tank that isn't empty yet stays as it is. Once all the valves on a deep reservoir's pipe are open, the station hears the pipe fill and sends a patrol to the reservoir. This is one of the command systems and runs after the mission system (it reads and adds to the mission state). Dragging and connecting the hoses is done by the simulation (TankSystem). Doesn't allocate. api/LastFleet.AI.Missions.html.summary: Namespace LastFleet.AI.Missions Classes BattleStations A boarded warship's crew at battle stations (design doc, "Boarding action: a ship in the fight"; boarding.crew in campaign.json): the ship knows it's been boarded the moment the pod clamps on, so it never drops below high alert, every soldier is on the move between rooms rather than standing at a post, hunters are sent sooner and given no breathers, and they push the squad harder once they find it. BoardingPlan A boarding action's warship (design doc, "Boarding action: a ship in the fight"): where its gun batteries, its reactor and its fire suppression controls are, how the fight outside goes (how often the fleet's guns hit it, what a hit does, how fires spread and are put out, how hard its batteries hit the fleet), and how its crew fights. BreachPlan A hull breach (HullBreaches): the plate that covers it, the plate's bounds, and which direction points into the room. BreachTuning How windows onto space break and what a breach does (content/defs/breaches.json, docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 10), the same for every mission: how much a window takes before it's blown out and when its cracks show, how hard and how far the air rushing out pulls, what it does to anyone beside it and what it drags out, and how long the compartment's doors take to seal, the shutter to close and the compartment to repressurize; and how it looks (the shutter's drop, the mist streaming out, the lamps over sealed doors). Whether a breach is for good is the mission recipe's (its breaches block). CargoPodSystem Runs cargo pod defenses (CargoPod). Once the drone is called, it takes longer to arrive the deeper into the station the squad is (DefenseSeconds(in MissionState)), and the station comes for the pod. ClosetPlan A spawn closet: its door part and bounds, the spots where soldiers spawn inside, and the closet's interior bounds. MissionPlan A level's mission layout: keycards and locks, the terminal, the extraction point, spawn closets, fallback points where reinforcements can enter when no closet works, hull breaches the horde can come through, and fuel and water tanks to pump into the docked dropship. MissionSystem A boarding action (design doc, "Boarding action: a ship in the fight"): the warship the squad is on is in a fight with the fleet. The fleet's guns hit it on a cadence (each hit counted in HitCount, so everyone aboard feels it); a hit hurts those near it, and sometimes starts a fire or blows a window. Fires spread room to room and burn out, unless the ship's fire suppression is running: its sprinklers put them out, until a hit knocks it out (repaired at its controls in damage control) or its power goes (cutting the reactor kills it). While its batteries fire, the fleet takes damage. The squad silences the batteries and cuts the reactor by holding Interact at each, then takes the bridge; a battery or the reactor lost with its room to a breach is out for good. MissionTuning Mission tuning values. Distances are in meters, times in seconds. MissionWalk Whether the mission can still be finished with some compartments, or rooms, lost (docs/plans/structure-first.md, decision 8): from the insertion, through doorways whose rooms are both kept, each gate passable once its keycard's room has been reached and the way out once the objective has, can the objective and then an extraction be reached? A breach seals its compartment for good only when this holds without it and every compartment already lost, so two losses can never together lock the squad out, and keycards stay reachable whatever is sealed. ObjectivePlan What a mission's squad comes for and how long it takes (docs/plans/structure-first.md, "Objective kinds"): the hack, a download whose drive is carried out, or a self-destruct counted down while the squad gets off. PatrolRoomPlan A room the Director's patrols can come out of when no spawn closet will do (a security office, crew quarters): only while nobody is in it, near its spots or can see one, its zone open and its compartment unsealed. RoomDoorTuning How rooms' own doors behave (content/defs/doors.json, docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 10), the same for every mission: how near someone comes for a sliding door to open and how long it waits to shut behind them; how near a player reaches a door opened by hand, and how long a soldier takes to open one on his way; and how much battering a door opened by hand takes from the swarm before it's broken open for good. TankPlan A fuel or water tank in the mission (SupplyTank), with its starting state. TankPumpSystem Pumps supply tanks (SupplyTank) into the docked dropship. Whatever gets pumped belongs to the fleet immediately (Delivered), even if the mission fails afterward. ThreatPlan How hard a level's places are defended (docs/plans/structure-first.md, "Threat drives the fight"), and the patrols that sets. While the squad is in a room, its threat sets how often the Director sends a patrol and how big, the station's alert speeding both on top. Structs BulkheadPlan A door through a bulkhead that seals (docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 8): the level part that fills its doorway, its bounds, and the compartments either side of it. EscapePodPlan An escape pod: the level part (surface) of its hatch and the hatch's bounds, the middle of the pod inside, and how many it seats. FirePanel A boarded warship's fire suppression panel (design doc, "Boarding action: a ship in the fight"): holding Interact at it floods its room while it burns, putting the fire out. MissionKeyPlan A keycard placed in the level. It opens the lock with the same id. MissionLockPlan A locked door: the level part (surface) that fills its doorway, plus its bounds. ReinforcementPoint A spawn point for reinforcements, with a yaw that faces into the level. RoomDoorPlan A room's own door in a plan's level, as the mission runs it (docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 10): its part, the rooms either side, and whether it's opened by hand or slides open for whoever comes near. SuppressionControls A boarded warship's fire suppression controls (design doc, "Boarding action: a ship in the fight"), in its damage control: while the system runs, the ship's sprinklers put its fires out; a hit can knock it out, and holding Interact here repairs it. WindowPlan A window onto space, as the mission's breaches need it (docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 10): its parts by surface, where its pane is, the compartment it lets space into, and whether that may ever be lost.

api/LastFleet.AI.Navigation.NavClusters..summary: Class NavClusters Namespace LastFleet.AI.Navigation Assembly LastFleet.AI.dll A coarse map over a NavGrid for long paths. Each 4 m square of each floor is split into clusters of walkable cells that connect inside the square, and clusters are linked wherever a link or a drop crosses from one to the next. public sealed class NavClusters Inheritance object NavClusters Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks A search over clusters (a few thousand in a big level, versus hundreds of thousands of cells) finds which ones a path goes through, and the cell search then stays inside those. That crosses a whole deck in a few thousand steps instead of visiting every reachable cell. Any cell in a cluster can reach any other without leaving it (they're connected by straight links inside the square), so a chain of linked clusters always contains a path. Built of the floor as the grid was built (WasBuiltWalkable(int)), and never changed after: it's part of the grid's NavTopology, shared by every Pathfinder on it. The search over it, with its memory, is each pathfinder's own (LastFleet.AI.Navigation.CorridorSearch). api/LastFleet.AI.Navigation.NavGrid.html.title: Class NavGrid | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.AI.Navigation.NavGrid.html.summary: Class NavGrid Namespace LastFleet.AI.Navigation Assembly LastFleet.AI.dll A layered navigation grid over a level. Each column of the grid holds every floor in it, from the ground up to mezzanines, catwalks and stair landings, so floors stacked over each other are all navigable. public sealed class NavGrid Inheritance object NavGrid Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks A cell is one floor in one column. Cells are numbered column by column, bottom floor first, so a cell number is no longer z * Width + x; use CellX(int), CellZ(int) and Column(int, int). Sampling: a ray down each column finds the top surface. The ray then restarts just under it and passes out of the solid without hitting anything (faces are one-sided), finds the next surface down, and so on. A surface counts as floor when it's flat enough and an upward ray finds headroom. Below the top surface, that upward ray has to hit the underside of something before it reaches the surface above. If it doesn't, the surface is inside a solid (the floor under a wall or crate) and isn't floor. Every collider is a closed box, so open air always has an underside above it. Each floor cell links to the floor in each of its eight neighboring columns that's within a step of its height. A cell is walkable when it's floor and every column within the agent's radius has floor reachable by steps, so agents keep their distance from walls and edges. Walkable cells at a ledge also get one-way drop links to walkable floor below, up to MaxDropHeight. Fields MaxLayers Maximum number of floors kept per column. public const int MaxLayers = 8 Field Value int Properties CellCount Number of cells (floors across all columns). public int CellCount { get; } Property Value int CellSize public float CellSize { get; } Property Value float Depth Columns along Z. public int Depth { get; } Property Value int DropCount Number of drop links, from a ledge to the floor below. public int DropCount { get; } Property Value int HasObstacles True once an obstacle placed after the grid was built covers some of its cells. public bool HasObstacles { get; } Property Value bool ObstacleVersion Changes whenever obstacles are placed or cleared, so what depends on them knows to look again. public int ObstacleVersion { get; } Property Value int Origin World X and Z of the corner of column 0. public Vector2 Origin { get; } Property Value Vector2 StepHeight public float StepHeight { get; } Property Value float Topology What never changes about this grid's navigation (each cell's coordinates, the cluster map), built the first time it's asked for and then shared by every Pathfinder on the grid. It's of the floor as built, so obstacles placed later don't change it. public NavTopology Topology { get; } Property Value NavTopology WalkableCount Number of walkable cells. public int WalkableCount { get; } Property Value int Width Columns along X. public int Width { get; } Property Value int Methods Build(ICollisionWorld, Vector3, Vector3) Samples world over the box from min to max. public static NavGrid Build(ICollisionWorld world, Vector3 min, Vector3 max) Parameters world ICollisionWorld min Vector3 max Vector3 Returns NavGrid Build(ICollisionWorld, Vector3, Vector3, NavGridSettings) Samples world over the box from min to max. public static NavGrid Build(ICollisionWorld world, Vector3 min, Vector3 max, NavGridSettings settings) Parameters world ICollisionWorld min Vector3 max Vector3 settings NavGridSettings Returns NavGrid CanStep(int, int) Returns true if an agent can walk directly between two walkable cells in neighboring columns. public bool CanStep(int from, int to) Parameters from int to int Returns bool CellOf(Vector3) Returns the cell under position (feet, or a point just above them): the highest floor in its column that's no more than half a meter above it. Returns -1 outside the grid or below every floor. public int CellOf(Vector3 position) Parameters position Vector3 Returns int CellX(int) public int CellX(int cell) Parameters cell int Returns int CellZ(int) public int CellZ(int cell) Parameters cell int Returns int CenterOf(int) Returns the center of a cell's floor. public Vector3 CenterOf(int cell) Parameters cell int Returns Vector3 ClearObstacles() Clears every mark made by SetObstacle(int, bool). public void ClearObstacles() Column(int, int) Returns the cells of the column at (x, z): its floors, bottom first. public (int First, int Count) Column(int x, int z) Parameters x int z int Returns (int Min, int Max) Direction(int) Returns the column offset for a neighbor direction. public static (int X, int Z) Direction(int direction) Parameters direction int Returns (int Min, int Max) DropsFrom(int) Returns the walkable floor cells below a ledge that an agent can drop to from cell. public ReadOnlySpan<int> DropsFrom(int cell) Parameters cell int Returns ReadOnlySpan<int> HasClearLine(int, int) True if an agent can walk in a straight line between two cells: every column the line crosses has walkable floor linked by steps to the last, ending on to itself rather than a floor above or below it. Used to smooth paths and to check strafe room. public bool HasClearLine(int from, int to) Parameters from int to int Returns bool HasClearLine(int, int, bool[]?) As HasClearLine(int, int), and the line crosses no cell marked in shut (one entry per cell, such as a pathfinder's shut doors), so a smoothed path doesn't cut through a shut door. public bool HasClearLine(int from, int to, bool[]? shut) Parameters from int to int shut bool[] Returns bool HeightAt(int) Returns the floor height of a cell. public float HeightAt(int cell) Parameters cell int Returns float IsWalkable(int) public bool IsWalkable(int cell) Parameters cell int Returns bool NearestWalkable(Vector3, float) Returns the walkable cell nearest position within maxRadius meters horizontally, on a floor from 2.5 m below to half a meter above it, or -1. That range means a point in the air finds the floor under it, not the story above or below. public int NearestWalkable(Vector3 position, float maxRadius = 3) Parameters position Vector3 maxRadius float Returns int Remarks Walkable floor at the point's own height within 1.5 m is preferred. That way someone at the edge of a catwalk (too close to the railing to be walkable) is placed on the catwalk, not on the floor beneath it. Neighbor(int, int) Returns the floor in the neighboring column in direction (0 to 7: +X, -X, +Z, -Z, then the diagonals) that's within a step of this cell's height, or -1. public int Neighbor(int cell, int direction) Parameters cell int direction int Returns int SetObstacle(int, bool) Marks a cell as covered by an obstacle placed after the grid was built, so nothing walks there, or clears the mark. A cell that wasn't walkable stays unwalkable. public void SetObstacle(int cell, bool obstacle) Parameters cell int obstacle bool WasBuiltWalkable(int) Whether a cell was walkable as the grid was built, whatever obstacles have been placed since. public bool WasBuiltWalkable(int cell) Parameters cell int Returns bool

api/LastFleet.AI.Soldiers.SoldierTuning..summary: Class SoldierTuning Namespace LastFleet.AI.Soldiers Assembly LastFleet.AI.dll How tough soldiers are to fight. Difficulty comes from reactions, aim and coordination, never from health (see the Difficulty table in the design doc). public sealed record SoldierTuning : IEquatable<SoldierTuning> Inheritance object SoldierTuning Implements IEquatable<SoldierTuning> Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Properties AimDownSightsRange Beyond this distance a soldier aims down sights, in meters. public float AimDownSightsRange { get; init; } Property Value float AimErrorPerTargetSpeed Extra aim error per meter per second of target speed, in degrees. Moving players are harder to hit. public float AimErrorPerTargetSpeed { get; init; } Property Value float AimSettleSeconds public float AimSettleSeconds { get; init; } Property Value float AmbushMemorySeconds How long a squad waits in ambush behind a door it can't open, for an enemy it knows is on the other side, in seconds. public float AmbushMemorySeconds { get; init; } Property Value float BoundDistance Farthest a soldier moves in one bound when advancing or falling back, in meters. It moves from cover to the next cover while the rest of the squad covers it, then the next soldier goes. public float BoundDistance { get; init; } Property Value float BurstPauseSeconds Pause between bursts, in seconds. public (float Min, float Max) BurstPauseSeconds { get; init; } Property Value (float Min, float Max) CalloutRange A soldier that spots an enemy tells squadmates within this range, in meters. public float CalloutRange { get; init; } Property Value float CloseAwarenessRange public float CloseAwarenessRange { get; init; } Property Value float CloseQuartersRange Indoors, within this range of the enemy, soldiers fight at close quarters: cover and fighting distances shrink to fit the room. public float CloseQuartersRange { get; init; } Property Value float ContainSeconds How much longer than RoomHoldSeconds a squad placed to guard the station contains the enemy in a room before going in after him, in seconds. Reinforcements and patrols don't wait. public float ContainSeconds { get; init; } Property Value float ConvergeRooms A squad that spots the enemy alerts soldiers this many rooms away (counting doorways), on top of those within CalloutRange, so neighboring squads converge on the fight. public int ConvergeRooms { get; init; } Property Value int CoverRouteClearance The straight route to a cover point has to pass at least this far from the enemy, in meters. Soldiers don't run past you or toward you to reach cover. public float CoverRouteClearance { get; init; } Property Value float CoverSearchRadius How far a soldier looks for cover, in meters. public float CoverSearchRadius { get; init; } Property Value float Default public static SoldierTuning Default { get; } Property Value SoldierTuning DeliberateMissDegrees How far off a soldier without the right to shoot to kill aims, in degrees. public float DeliberateMissDegrees { get; init; } Property Value float FieldOfViewDegrees Full width of the view cone, in degrees. Anything within CloseAwarenessRange is noticed no matter which direction it's in. public float FieldOfViewDegrees { get; init; } Property Value float FireTeamSize Indoors, the level's squads (often one or two soldiers per room) are merged into fire teams of up to this many, from neighboring rooms, so they cover, suppress, flank and take rooms together. 0 or 1 leaves them as placed. public int FireTeamSize { get; init; } Property Value int FireToleranceDegrees Only fire when the aim is within this many degrees of the target point. public float FireToleranceDegrees { get; init; } Property Value float GrenadeChancePerSecond Chance per second, once a grenade is warranted, that an eligible soldier throws one. public float GrenadeChancePerSecond { get; init; } Property Value float GrenadeHidingSeconds Seconds the enemy has to be out of the squad's sight before a grenade is considered. public float GrenadeHidingSeconds { get; init; } Property Value float HearingRange Enemy gunfire within this range is heard, in meters. public float HearingRange { get; init; } Property Value float InitialAimErrorDegrees Aim error at first sight, in degrees. It settles toward SettledAimErrorDegrees over AimSettleSeconds. public float InitialAimErrorDegrees { get; init; } Property Value float LoseSightSeconds Seconds without line of sight before a soldier starts hunting. public float LoseSightSeconds { get; init; } Property Value float MaxCoverAngleDegrees Cover more than this many degrees around from the soldier's side of the enemy (as seen from the enemy) isn't considered, since it would mean getting behind you. Flankers aim for wide angles under this limit. public float MaxCoverAngleDegrees { get; init; } Property Value float MaxPoise The most resistance sustained fire can build. Hits still stagger a little at the cap. public float MaxPoise { get; init; } Property Value float MaxSearchSeconds Maximum seconds a soldier searches for a lost enemy before standing down, no matter what's left to check. public float MaxSearchSeconds { get; init; } Property Value float MaxShootersPerTarget Maximum soldiers allowed to shoot to kill at one target at the same time. The rest still fire, but deliberately miss by DeliberateMissDegrees, so their near misses suppress and threaten without stacking up damage. Soldiers take turns, so the pressure moves around the squad. public int MaxShootersPerTarget { get; init; } Property Value int MaxStaggerSeconds The longest a single hit can stagger, in seconds. public float MaxStaggerSeconds { get; init; } Property Value float MinStaggerShare Hits smaller than this fraction of a soldier's health don't stagger it (every hit still plays a flinch on screen). Headshots and heavy rounds (hand cannon, shotgun, marksman rifle) stagger; a rifle's body shots don't. public float MinStaggerShare { get; init; } Property Value float Remarks When every hit staggered, soldiers lost over a quarter of their damage output in the room benchmark. PoisePerShare Stagger resistance gained per fraction of health taken. Each hit staggers for (1 - poise) times as long. public float PoisePerShare { get; init; } Property Value float PoiseRecovery How fast the resistance wears off, per second. public float PoiseRecovery { get; init; } Property Value float PreferredRange Preferred fighting distance band, in meters. Closer than this it backs off, farther it advances. public (float Min, float Max) PreferredRange { get; init; } Property Value (float Min, float Max) PushRange How close a push gets to the enemy, in meters. public float PushRange { get; init; } Property Value float ReactionSeconds Time from first noticing an enemy to acting on it, in seconds (randomized between min and max). public (float Min, float Max) ReactionSeconds { get; init; } Property Value (float Min, float Max) RoamGiveUpSeconds It gives up on a spot it hasn't reached in this long, in seconds. public float RoamGiveUpSeconds { get; init; } Property Value float RoamRadius Min and max distance from its post that a roaming soldier walks to, in meters. public (float Min, float Max) RoamRadius { get; init; } Property Value (float Min, float Max) RoamShare Fraction of soldiers (not counting patrols or reinforcements) that wander around their post while idle. public float RoamShare { get; init; } Property Value float RoamWaitSeconds How long it stops at each spot to look around, in seconds. public (float Min, float Max) RoamWaitSeconds { get; init; } Property Value (float Min, float Max) RoamWalk Walking speed while roaming, as a fraction of full speed. public float RoamWalk { get; init; } Property Value float RoomHoldSeconds How long a squad holds a doorway, waiting for the enemy to come through, before it goes in, in seconds. public (float Min, float Max) RoomHoldSeconds { get; init; } Property Value (float Min, float Max) RoomPlanMemorySeconds How long a squad keeps hunting an enemy it lost before giving up on its room plan, in seconds. public float RoomPlanMemorySeconds { get; init; } Property Value float RoomPlanMinSquad Minimum soldiers a squad needs alive to go into a room. With fewer, it holds the doorway and keeps him in. public int RoomPlanMinSquad { get; init; } Property Value int RoomTactics Indoors (a generated level's rooms), instead of following a lost enemy through a doorway one at a time, a squad holds the doorway he went through, then stacks up beside it, throws a grenade in and goes in together. Its flanker goes through another doorway if there is one. public bool RoomTactics { get; init; } Property Value bool SearchSeconds Seconds a searching soldier looks around before standing down, once its squad has nothing left to check (every guess about where the enemy went has been checked, or none were made). public float SearchSeconds { get; init; } Property Value float SeparationDistance Soldiers keep at least this far apart, in meters. public float SeparationDistance { get; init; } Property Value float SettledAimErrorDegrees public float SettledAimErrorDegrees { get; init; } Property Value float ShooterRestSeconds public float ShooterRestSeconds { get; init; } Property Value float ShooterTurnSeconds How long a soldier keeps the right to shoot to kill (ShooterTurnSeconds), then how long it rests before asking again (ShooterRestSeconds), in seconds. public float ShooterTurnSeconds { get; init; } Property Value float SightRange How far a soldier can see, in meters. public float SightRange { get; init; } Property Value float SquadGrenadeCooldownSeconds Minimum seconds between two grenades from the same squad. public float SquadGrenadeCooldownSeconds { get; init; } Property Value float StaggerPerShare Seconds a hit staggers a soldier per fraction of its health the hit took (a hit for a fifth of its health staggers for 0.2 × this). While staggered it can't fire, stumbles back, and its aim gets knocked off and unsettled. public float StaggerPerShare { get; init; } Property Value float SuppressedHearingRange A suppressed shot is only heard in the room it's fired in. Where there are no rooms (or outside them), it's heard within this range instead, in meters. public float SuppressedHearingRange { get; init; } Property Value float SuppressionMemorySeconds How long a suppressor keeps firing at the enemy's last known position, in seconds. public float SuppressionMemorySeconds { get; init; } Property Value float SuppressionSeconds How long a near miss keeps a soldier suppressed, in seconds. public float SuppressionSeconds { get; init; } Property Value float TurnRate Turn speed, in radians per second. Fast enough to fight, slow enough that flanking pays off. public float TurnRate { get; init; } Property Value float

api/LastFleet.AI.Soldiers.html.title: Namespace LastFleet.AI.Soldiers | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.AI.Soldiers.html.summary: Namespace LastFleet.AI.Soldiers Classes SoldierAiSystem Barks, and picking an intent through utility scoring. SoldierArms Picks the guns soldiers carry. Each soldier's gun is derived from its seed, so the host and every client agree. SoldierSpawner Spawns soldiers with their AI. Each one is an enemy variant (EnemyRoster), which sets its body, guns, faction and the behavior it uses. SoldierTuning How tough soldiers are to fight. Difficulty comes from reactions, aim and coordination, never from health (see the Difficulty table in the design doc). SoldierTunings Soldier tuning per faction: the values every faction shares (Shared), plus separate values for any faction that differs (For(FactionId)). TuningField One soldier tuning value (SoldierTuning): its key in tuning.json, how it's shown and edited, and how it's read from and written to a tuning. The developer overlay, LastFleet Studio and the file all go through All, so they always agree on which fields exist. TuningFields Every soldier tuning value (SoldierTuning), grouped the way they're edited. This is the list of what tuning.json can hold and what the developer overlay and LastFleet Studio show, with slider ranges and a description of each. Structs CoverWork What choosing cover cost in a tick (LastCoverWork): how many choices, the cover points they looked at, the claim checks against other soldiers' cover, and the ray tests. For the developer overlay and the headless benchmark; the simulation never reads it. SightWork What looking for enemies cost in a tick (LastSightWork): how many soldiers looked, the characters they looked over, how many enemies were in view and range, and the sight lines cast to them. For the developer overlay and the headless benchmark; the simulation never reads it. Enums AiSection A part of SoldierAiSystem's tick, timed separately (LastMilliseconds(AiSection)). Together they are the whole tick. PathPurpose What a soldier's path search was for, to count the searches by (PathSearches). TuningKind The type of value a TuningField holds, which decides how it's saved and edited.

api/LastFleet.AI.Utility.UtilityInput.ht.summary: Enum UtilityInput Namespace LastFleet.AI.Utility Assembly LastFleet.AI.dll The inputs a soldier's curves and conditions can read when it scores its intents. public enum UtilityInput : byte Fields OwnHealth = 0 The soldier's own health, 0 to 1. TargetHealth = 1 The target's health, 0 to 1, or -1 if the soldier can't see the target. Range = 2 Distance to the target's last known position, in meters. SinceSeen = 3 Seconds since the squad last saw the target. Suppressed = 4 1 while near misses have the soldier pinned, otherwise 0. CoveringFire = 5 1 while the squad's suppressor is firing (and this soldier isn't the suppressor), otherwise 0. TargetReloading = 6 1 if the soldier can see the target reloading, otherwise 0. SquadPushing = 7 1 if a squadmate is already pushing, otherwise 0. Role = 8 The soldier's squad role, as a number (SquadRole). AdvanceBlocked = 9 1 if the soldier can't bound forward right now, otherwise 0. That's either because it isn't its turn (soldiers farther back go first) or because it recently found no cover ahead to bound to. SearchLeads = 10 How many of the squad's guesses about where a lost enemy went haven't been checked yet (Search for the enemy). 0 if they're all checked or none were made. Score = 11 The intent's running score while its terms are being added up. Always the last input.

api/LastFleet.Audio.AudioEngine.html.summary: Class AudioEngine Namespace LastFleet.Audio Assembly LastFleet.Audio.dll Plays sounds through OpenAL Soft. public sealed class AudioEngine : ISoundOutput, IDisposable Inheritance object AudioEngine Implements ISoundOutput IDisposable Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks There's a fixed set of voices (VoicePool). Each voice is a source with a low-pass filter for sounds heard through walls. Spatial voices send to one shared reverb, set by the kind of space the listener is in. Sounds placed in the world fade with distance and get dulled by the air. Effects, interface and ambience each have a volume, under a master volume. With no sound device (a server, or a machine with no output) it plays nothing and costs nothing. In offline mode (OpenOffline(SoundLibrary)) it mixes into memory instead of a device, which the smoke run and the tests use. Everything runs on the calling thread, and OpenAL Soft does its mixing on its own thread. Doesn't allocate after it opens. api/LastFleet.Audio.html.summary: Namespace LastFleet.Audio Classes AudioEngine Plays sounds through OpenAL Soft. PlaceholderSounds Stand-in sounds generated in code for everything the game plays, until a recording replaces them (a .wav in content/sounds, see docs/sound.md). SoundClip One recording (or placeholder) of a cue, as mono samples from -1 to 1. SoundCue How a sound plays, as defined in content/defs/sounds.json: how loud it is, how far it carries, whether it's placed in the world, and how many copies can play at once. SoundLibrary Every sound the game can play. Holds the cues (content/defs/sounds.json) and each cue's clips. The clips are the recordings in content/sounds (name.wav, name_2.wav, ...), or the cue's placeholder (PlaceholderSounds) until recordings exist. Each play picks one of the cue's clips at random. VoicePool Picks which of a fixed set of voices plays each new sound. Doesn't allocate. WavFile Reads and writes .wav files. Reads PCM 8, 16, 24 or 32-bit, or 32-bit float, mixed down to one channel. Interfaces ISoundOutput Where the game sends the sounds it wants played. That's AudioEngine, or a recorder in tests. Enums RoomAcoustics The kind of space the listener is in, for the reverb. SoundCategory Which volume setting controls a sound.

api/LastFleet.Content.Creatures.Animated.summary: Class AnimatedModel Namespace LastFleet.Content.Creatures Assembly LastFleet.Content.dll A creature made and animated in Blender (content/models, docs/blender/creatures.md): its meshes skinned to an armature and its actions, baked when loaded into where every vertex is on every frame, so the GPU can draw hundreds of them at once, each on its own frame, with no skinning of its own. public sealed class AnimatedModel Inheritance object AnimatedModel Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks The file's meshes are the body near (Lods[0]) and, those named *_LOD1, far away (Lods[1]; the near one again when there is none). Each animation is sampled at FramesPerSecond, from its start to its end inclusive. Translation, rotation (slerped) and scale of any node may be animated, with linear or step interpolation (a cubic spline is followed through its keys, linearly). Skinned meshes follow their joints (up to four a vertex); other meshes follow their own node. Faces are flat: each triangle has its own three vertices, and its normal is worked out again on every frame. api/LastFleet.Content.Loading.GltfMeshLo.summary: Class GltfMeshLoader Namespace LastFleet.Content.Loading Assembly LastFleet.Content.dll Loads a glTF level module into one flat-shaded, world-space MeshData, ready to draw and to build collision from. public static class GltfMeshLoader Inheritance object GltfMeshLoader Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Walks the file's scene, placing every triangle primitive with its node's transform. Each triangle gets a face normal computed after the transform, which is the grey-box look and makes the file's own normals irrelevant. Box = 2 One box around everything drawn, in the model's own axes. Cylinder = 3 One upright cylinder around everything drawn, standing on its base: for barrels and drums. Rays hit a 24-sided prism of the same size, within 1% of its radius. None = 4 Nothing: drawn only. Walked and shot through. Remarks Characters, shots, sight, cover and the navigation grid all use the same collider, so what you walk into, shoot and plan paths around agree. A model that breaks takes damage through one solid part, so it can only be Authored, Box or Cylinder; any other kind keeps its authored box.

api/LastFleet.Content.Rigs.RigTranslatio.summary: Enum RigTranslation Namespace LastFleet.Content.Rigs Assembly LastFleet.Content.dll Where a bone's offset from its parent comes from when a clip plays on a model of the rig (like Unreal's bone translation retargeting). This lets models on the same rig have different builds, such as longer arms or a shorter body, and still share its clips. public enum RigTranslation Fields Skeleton = 0 The model's own offset, as modeled. The clip rotates the bone but never stretches it. Animation = 1 The clip's offset, as animated. Used for bones that slide. Scaled = 2 The clip's offset, scaled by the ratio of the model's rest offset to the clip's. Used for the hips, so a taller body's hips bob and drop by the same amount relative to its size.

Create it once and reuse it every frame; nothing here allocates. public sealed class Pose Inheritance object Pose Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Constructors Pose(Skeleton) Creates a pose of skeleton in its rest pose. public Pose(Skeleton skeleton) Parameters skeleton Skeleton Properties Locals Each joint's transform relative to its parent. public Span<JointTransform> Locals { get; } Property Value Span<JointTransform> Skeleton The skeleton this pose is for. public Skeleton Skeleton { get; } Property Value Skeleton Methods Add(Pose, Pose, float, ReadOnlySpan<float>) Adds the difference between additive and reference to this pose, scaled by amount. Used for a lean, an aim offset or a kick authored as a clip from a neutral pose, on top of whatever the body is doing. With mask, each joint only gets as much as its weight. public void Add(Pose additive, Pose reference, float amount, ReadOnlySpan<float> mask = default) Parameters additive Pose reference Pose amount float mask ReadOnlySpan<float> Blend(Pose, float, ReadOnlySpan<float>) Moves this pose amount of the way toward other (0 is none, 1 is all of it). Used to blend two clips or fade from one to the next. With mask (one weight per joint, from Mask(IEnumerable<string>)), each joint only moves as far as its weight allows, for layering such as a reload over the legs running. public void Blend(Pose other, float amount, ReadOnlySpan<float> mask = default) Parameters other Pose amount float mask ReadOnlySpan<float> CopyFrom(Pose) Copies other, which must be a pose of the same skeleton. public void CopyFrom(Pose other) Parameters other Pose ModelSpace(Span<Matrix4x4>) Writes each joint's model-space transform (from joint space to model space) into joints. public void ModelSpace(Span<Matrix4x4> joints) Parameters joints Span<Matrix4x4> Reset() Resets to the skeleton's rest pose. public void Reset() Skin(in Matrix4x4, Span<Matrix4x4>) Writes the skinning matrices for this pose into matrices (one per joint) for the GPU, with the model placed in the world by placement. Each joint's matrix is its inverse bind, then its pose, then the placement. A skinned vertex is the weighted sum of its joints' matrices applied to it. public void Skin(in Matrix4x4 placement, Span<Matrix4x4> matrices) Parameters placement Matrix4x4 matrices Span<Matrix4x4>

api/LastFleet.Content.Skeletal.PoseIk.ht.summary: Class PoseIk Namespace LastFleet.Content.Skeletal Assembly LastFleet.Content.dll Inverse kinematics on a Pose: a two-bone chain (an arm, a leg) reaching for a point, rotating a chain (the spine and head looking up), and moving a joint (dropping the hips). public static class PoseIk Inheritance object PoseIk Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Each method works in model space and writes the joints' local transforms back. joints is the pose's model-space transforms (ModelSpace(Span<Matrix4x4>)), and every call keeps it up to date. Methods FromTo(Vector3, Vector3) Returns the shortest rotation that turns direction from onto to. public static Quaternion FromTo(Vector3 from, Vector3 to) Parameters from Vector3 to Vector3 Returns Quaternion Reach(Pose, Span<Matrix4x4>, int, int, int, Vector3, Vector3, float) Bends the chain root, middle, tip (each the parent of the next) so the tip reaches target, or gets as close as the chain's length allows. api/LastFleet.Content.Skeletal.SkinnedMo.summary: Class SkinnedModel Namespace LastFleet.Content.Skeletal Assembly LastFleet.Content.dll A character made in Blender on a rig (content/characters, see docs/blender/rigs.md). Properties Materials The model's materials, with their Blender colors. Paint slots are the ones named Paint_<Slot>. public IReadOnlyList<ModelMaterial> Materials { get; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<ModelMaterial> Skeleton The skeleton that drives the model. public Skeleton Skeleton { get; } Property Value Skeleton VertexMaterials Each vertex's material, as an index into Materials. public ReadOnlySpan<int> VertexMaterials { get; } Property Value ReadOnlySpan<int> Vertices The model's triangles, three vertices each, in the colors from the file. public ReadOnlySpan<SkinnedVertex> Vertices { get; } Property Value ReadOnlySpan<SkinnedVertex> Methods Colored(ReadOnlySpan<Vector3>) Returns the vertices with each material recolored from colors (one per Materials; values above 1 glow), for a variant's paint. Materials past the end of the span keep the file's color. public SkinnedVertex[] Colored(ReadOnlySpan<Vector3> colors) Parameters colors ReadOnlySpan<Vector3> Returns SkinnedVertex[] Load(string, MaterialLibrary?) Loads the skinned meshes in path (.gltf or .glb) that use the file's first skin. public static SkinnedModel Load(string path, MaterialLibrary? library = null) Parameters path string The file. library MaterialLibrary The library to look materials up in. It uses the matrices from Skin(in Matrix4x4, Span<Matrix4x4>), and each vertex is the weighted sum of its joints' matrices applied to it. into gets one vertex for each of Vertices, with each face lit by its own normal. Doesn't allocate. public void Skin(ReadOnlySpan<Matrix4x4> matrices, Span<MeshVertex> into) Parameters matrices ReadOnlySpan<Matrix4x4> into Span<MeshVertex>

api/LastFleet.Content.Skeletal.html.summary: Namespace LastFleet.Content.Skeletal Namespaces LastFleet.Content.Skeletal.Graph Classes ClipSet A rig's clips (content/anim/<rig>.gltf: the armature and its actions, made in Blender), bound to a skeleton by joint name so every model of the rig can play them. Channels for joints the skeleton doesn't have are dropped. Pose The transform of every joint of a Skeleton relative to its parent, from one sampled clip or several blended together. Create it once and reuse it every frame; nothing here allocates. PoseIk Inverse kinematics on a Pose: a two-bone chain (an arm, a leg) reaching for a point, rotating a chain (the spine and head looking up), and moving a joint (dropping the hips). RigFit Checks whether a model fits its rig: it must have the rig's bones under the same parents, and its eye must be where the simulation expects it. SkeletalClip One of a rig's clips (an action made in Blender), bound to a Skeleton. It holds the keys for each joint it moves. It can be sampled into a Pose at any time, interpolating between keys, so it plays at any rate. Skeleton The joints that drive a skinned model (a glTF skin: the armature made in Blender on a rig), ordered so each comes after its parent. It holds their names, their rest pose relative to their parents, and the inverse bind matrices that take a vertex from model space to each joint. SkinnedModel A character made in Blender on a rig (content/characters, see docs/blender/rigs.md). Its meshes are skinned to the rig's skeleton and stored as flat triangles in the bind pose, each vertex with its four joints and weights, so the GPU can skin it every frame using the pose the game provides. Structs JointPoint A point attached to a joint and bound to a skeleton, such as a rig socket (where a hand holds the gun, where the eye is). It stores the joint and the point in the joint's own space. JointTransform A joint's transform relative to its parent: translation, rotation and scale. SkinnedVertex A vertex of a skinned model in its rest (bind) pose, laid out the way the GPU reads it. It holds the position, the face normal (faces are flat), the color, the four joints that move it with their weights, and its surface data.

api/LastFleet.Core.Determinism.Determini.summary: Class DeterministicRandom Namespace LastFleet.Core.Determinism Assembly LastFleet.Core.dll A seeded pseudo-random generator (xoshiro256**) that produces the same sequence on every machine. public sealed class DeterministicRandom Inheritance object DeterministicRandom Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Simulation, procedural generation and loot code must use this type, never Random: the BCL generator's algorithm is an implementation detail that can change between .NET versions, and co-op peers regenerate levels and weapons from seeds alone. A stream depends only on the run seed and its name, so adding a roll in one generation pass never shifts the results of another. Not thread-safe. Use one instance per thread or job. Manufacturer string The manufacturer whose guns it can go on, or null for any. Rarity int The lowest rarity rank it can appear at. Weight double Pick weight. Archetypes IReadOnlyList<string> The archetype ids it fits. Empty means all. Mods IReadOnlyList<StatRange> The stat changes it applies. Model string The model it uses. Either a name in the frame's part file (Barrel_2_Heavy), or just the shape those names end with (Heavy) so one part picks its look on every frame. None means nothing is shown in the slot. For an optic it's the sight type (Iron, RedDot, Holographic, Scope). Null picks one based on the id. Paint IReadOnlyDictionary<string, Vector3> Colors for the model's paint slots (materials named Paint_<Slot>), keyed by slot. Slots not listed keep the model's own color. Null for none. Reticle string An optic's reticle (Reticles). Red dot and holographic sights use dot, ring or chevron; scopes use duplex, mildot or chevron. Null uses the sight's default. Traits WeaponTraits Extra effects beyond its stat changes, for example a suppressor's Suppressed. Since int The loot data generation the part was added in (0 for parts that existed before generations). A weapon only rolls from parts of its own generation or earlier (Generation), so adding a part to a pool doesn't change any weapon a player already has. api/LastFleet.Loot.Definitions.html.title: Namespace LastFleet.Loot.Definitions | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.Loot.Definitions.html.summary: Namespace LastFleet.Loot.Definitions Classes Affix A prefix ("Overclocked") or suffix ("of the Vigil") that can roll onto weapons of high enough rarity. Fabrication Something the armory can fabricate from graded material (the "fabrication" data). It's either a weapon rolled from a loot table or a weapon part (for one slot or any slot). The item level comes from the grade it costs. ItemTable What a pile, container or cargo crate holds (content/defs/loot/items.json, "itemTables"). A roll picks one entry by weight, plus a count. ItemTableEntry One entry in an ItemTable: an item, how likely it is to be picked, and how many drop. LootArchetype A weapon frame for loot rolls: the simulation's WeaponArchetype, the 0–100 stats a roll starts from, and the bounds every stat gets clamped to at the end. LootEntry One weighted entry in a loot table. It can only drop between its min and max item levels. LootTable A loot table: weighted entries (archetypes, nested tables, relics), plus biases on the rarity and manufacturer odds. The biases multiply down through nested tables. Manufacturer A weapon manufacturer: its stat bias, which applies to every gun it makes, and its model names per archetype. A manufacturer with no model for an archetype doesn't make that archetype. MaterialGrade A grade of refined material (the "grades" data: Mk I, Mk II, ...). The fleet's refinery makes it from raw materials, and the armory uses it to fabricate items. A higher grade gives a higher item level. Rarity A rarity tier. Its chance is Weight × (1 + PerLevel × (item level − 1)), times the loot table's bias. So higher item levels shift the odds toward rarer tiers. RefineryRecipe A refinery recipe for turning raw materials into a material grade (the "recipes" data). One batch uses Inputs and produces Count of Grade. RefineryTier One upgrade level of the fleet's refinery (the "refineryTiers" data, lowest first). A fleet starts at the first tier. Each tier has an upgrade cost paid from the fleet's stores, the grades it can make, and how many batches it refines per jump. Relic A hand-authored unique weapon with a fixed archetype, manufacturer, parts and affixes. Every range rolls at its best value. ReworkRules How the armory's workbench reworks what's in the locker (crafting.json's "rework"), paid in refined material. A weapon is reworked to a higher item level: the same roll, its stats at the new level, paid in the grade that makes things of that level. A part is tuned: its ranges roll better, paid in the grade of its rarity. SalvageYield What the armory's workbench gets from dismantling a weapon or a part of one rarity (crafting.json's "salvage"): raw materials, by item id, which go to the fleet's stores for the refinery. WeaponPart A weapon part in a slot's pool. Structs LootColor A HUD color, parsed from a #rrggbb value in the data. StatRange One stat change and the range it rolls in. If Multiply is false, it adds whole points to a 0–100 stat. If it's true, it multiplies the stat or scale. Additions are applied before multiplications. Enums FabricationKind What a Fabrication makes. LootEntryKind What a loot table entry drops. LootStat A stat that a weapon part, manufacturer or affix can change. The first five are 0–100 stats. The rest are scales on the frame's damage, magazine or zoom (see WeaponProfile). WeaponPartSlot The part slots on a weapon (see the design doc, "Weapon anatomy"). The first five are the original slots. Muzzle, grip and trigger were added later. They roll after everything else, each from its own random stream, so adding them didn't change any weapon rolled before (see Since).

api/LastFleet.Loot.Drops.LootSystem.html.summary: Class LootSystem Namespace LastFleet.Loot.Drops Assembly LastFleet.Loot.dll Handles soldier weapon and kit drops. When a soldier (anything with a LootDrop) dies, it can drop a weapon where it fell, and next to it a medkit or ammo pack, or a weapon part (each with its own separate roll). public sealed class LootSystem : ISimulationSystem Inheritance object LootSystem Implements ISimulationSystem Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks The weapon is rolled from the SoldierLoot table for the gun the soldier carried (the table id with ".archetype" appended, for example "loot.station.soldier.machine_gun"), or from the base table if there isn't one for that gun. api/LastFleet.Loot.Parts.PartFitSystem.h.summary: Class PartFitSystem Namespace LastFleet.Loot.Parts Assembly LastFleet.Loot.dll Handles fitting weapon parts, anywhere and at any time (FitPart). A part from the pack goes onto one of the two weapons, replacing the part in that slot, and the replaced part goes into the pack in its place. public sealed class PartFitSystem : ISimulationSystem Inheritance object PartFitSystem Implements ISimulationSystem Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Fitting takes the part's fit time (its item's fitSeconds) with the weapon lowered, and getting hit cancels it (the part stays in the pack). The weapon is rebuilt from its roll with the new part (Roll(WeaponIdentity)), so its stats, model and card update. The magazine and reserve keep what they hold, capped at the new sizes. This is a command system, because it needs the loot data, which the simulation doesn't have. It runs at the start of a tick, before the inventory system, which leaves an in-progress part fitting to it. Only rolled weapons take parts, and relics don't. It doesn't allocate except on the tick a part goes on. Constructors PartFitSystem(LootCatalog) Handles fitting weapon parts, anywhere and at any time (FitPart). api/LastFleet.Networking.Lobby.FleetRequ.title: Enum FleetRequestKind | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.Networking.Lobby.FleetRequ.summary: Enum FleetRequestKind Namespace LastFleet.Networking.Lobby Assembly LastFleet.Networking.dll What a joined player asks the host to do with the fleet. Everything at home is shared, so anyone in the lobby can ask; the host checks the request against its fleet and carries it out. public enum FleetRequestKind : byte Fields SetCourse = 1 Vote for a course: a system one jump away, or through the gate. Value is the system's id, or StarMap.GateExit. The course set is the one most of the squad picked. UpgradeRefinery = 2 Upgrade the refinery to its next tier, paid from the fleet's supplies. Fabricate = 3 Fabricate something into the armory's locker. Text is the fabrication's id. VoteJump = 4 Vote to jump on the course set (Value 1), or take the vote back (0). PickPoint = 5 Pick the point of interest in the fleet's system the squad drops to next. Value is its id. StoreWeapon = 6 Put the weapon in this player's hands in the locker (never their last). StorePart = 7 Put the part in this player's inventory slot Value in the locker. TakeItem = 8 Take locker item Value: a weapon into this player's hands (the one held goes in the locker if their hands are full), a part into their pack. FitPart = 9 Fit locker part Extra to locker weapon Value. RemovePart = 10 Take the part fitted in slot Extra off locker weapon Value. Dismantle = 11 Dismantle locker item Value into raw material for the refinery. Rework = 12 Rework locker item Value: a weapon up a few levels, a part tuned.

api/LastFleet.Networking.Lobby.RelayTran.summary: Class RelayTransport Namespace LastFleet.Networking.Lobby Assembly LastFleet.Networking.dll Wraps the lobby's connection for one mission. It joins the lobby (checking the version), keeps track of who's there and which mission is set up, and tells the host when this player is ready. When the host starts a mission, it gives the game a RelayTransport to use for the mission's NetClient. The connection stays open between missions. LobbyHost The host's lobby, where the squad gathers between missions. On its own it only holds the host. Once it's opened on a connection with Open(ITransport), friends can join, mark themselves ready, and see the mission the host has set up and what everyone is carrying. LobbyMember A player in a lobby, either the host (slot 0) or a client. RelayTransport Wraps the lobby's connection for one mission. The mission's NetHost or NetClient talks to this as if it were the real connection, while the lobby keeps the real one open between missions. Structs FleetAsk A fleet request that has reached the host, with the name of the lobby member who sent it. FleetRequest A joined player's request to the host about the shared fleet. LobbyEvent Something that happened in the lobby we joined, for the game to act on. LobbyWeapon A weapon a lobby member is taking into the next mission. Holds its name and rarity rank, which picks its color. Enums FleetRequestKind What a joined player asks the host to do with the fleet. Everything at home is shared, so anyone in the lobby can ask; the host checks the request against its fleet and carries it out. LobbyClientState The current state of a LobbyClient.
