api/LastFleet.Networking.Protocol.Messag.summary: Enum MessageType Namespace LastFleet.Networking.Protocol Assembly LastFleet.Networking.dll The first byte of every message. public enum MessageType : byte Fields Hello = 1 Client to host: protocol version and player name. The first message after connecting. Welcome = 2 Host to client: the client was accepted. Carries the player slot, entity and level. Reject = 3 Host to client: the client was refused, with the reason. The host disconnects after sending it. Input = 4 Client to host: the latest player commands, plus a few earlier ones in case packets get lost. Snapshot = 5 Host to client: the state of the world at a tick. Events = 6 Host to client: what happened on a tick (shots, hits, explosions, broken props, barks). LobbyWelcome = 7 Host to client: the reply to a lobby hello, with the player slot the client was given. LobbyState = 8 Host to client: who's in the lobby, whether they're ready, what they're carrying, and the next mission. LobbyReady = 9 Client to host: whether the player is ready for the mission. MissionStart = 10 Host to client: a mission is starting, with its level name. The client loads it and joins. MissionEnd = 11 Host to client: the mission is over, with how it went. The client goes back to the lobby. MissionLeave = 12 Client to host: the player is leaving the mission for the lobby. The others keep playing. MissionRejoin = 13 Client to host: the player wants to rejoin the running mission. FleetState = 14 Host to client: the whole fleet (its stores, ships, map and log), packed by FleetWire. Sent when a player joins and whenever the fleet changes, since everything at home is shared. FleetRequest = 15 Client to host: a request about the shared fleet (set a course, upgrade the refinery, fabricate). The host checks it, carries it out, and sends everyone the fleet again.

So the host leaves the entry unchanged until the client's guess is off by more than matters at that distance (10 cm at the client's feet, more farther away, and three times that for a character the client can't see), or the character has turned more than a few degrees, or changed speed. In between, the entry repeats what it said last time, which costs nothing after the delta against the client's last copy. Everything else about a character (health, stance, weapon, death) is always sent fresh. api/LastFleet.Networking.Replication.Sna.summary: Class SnapshotDelta Namespace LastFleet.Networking.Replication Assembly LastFleet.Networking.dll Delta compression for snapshots. Each snapshot is sent as a delta from one the client has acknowledged. Its bytes are XORed with the baseline's, so anything unchanged becomes zero, and the result is sent as runs: a count of unchanged bytes, then a count of changed bytes followed by those bytes, and so on. public static class SnapshotDelta Inheritance object SnapshotDelta Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks It doesn't know anything about what's in a snapshot apart from its sections. That works because the snapshot writer lays the world out the same way every tick: a soldier standing still costs nothing, and a moving one costs a few bytes of position. A snapshot starts with a table of its section lengths (BeginSections(NetWriter, int)), and each section is compared against the same section of the baseline. So when a list grows or shrinks, only the rest of that list shifts, not everything after it. Without a baseline (the first snapshot, or after a long stretch of packet loss), the delta from nothing is just the whole snapshot. Fields MaxSections The maximum number of sections in a snapshot. public const int MaxSections = 32 Field Value int Methods BeginSections(NetWriter, int) Starts a snapshot with sections sections by writing its section table, which EndSection(NetWriter, int, int, int) fills in as each section ends. Returns the offset where the first section starts. public static int BeginSections(NetWriter writer, int sections) Parameters writer NetWriter sections int Returns int Decode(ref NetReader, ReadOnlySpan<byte>, Span<byte>) Rebuilds a snapshot from its delta and the baseline it was encoded against. public static int Decode(ref NetReader reader, ReadOnlySpan<byte> baseline, Span<byte> output) Parameters reader NetReader baseline ReadOnlySpan<byte> output Span<byte> Returns int The snapshot's length in output. api/LastFleet.Networking.Replication.Swa.summary: Class SwarmView Namespace LastFleet.Networking.Replication Assembly LastFleet.Networking.dll What one client knows about the horde, kept on the host, and the horde's part of that client's snapshots. It stays within the design's budget (64 kbps for everything) no matter how many swarmlings there are. public sealed class SwarmView Inheritance object SwarmView Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks There are two parts. First a table of the swarmlings near the client (within Range), each in a slot it keeps while it stays near: their ids, then one bit each for the dead. The table only changes as swarmlings arrive, leave and die, so the delta against the client's last acknowledged snapshot costs almost nothing. Then come updates, packed to about 8 bytes each: where some of the swarmlings are (to 3 cm, relative to the client's feet), which way they're moving and facing, and what they're doing. Each snapshot gets as many updates as the client's budget has room for after the rest of the fight is sent (Fit(int)), between 2 and 16. With 300 nearby, each one gets updated about every one to four seconds. The client draws each swarmling along its updates (LastFleet.Networking.Replication.SwarmTrack), and the host keeps the same tracks, so it knows where the client is drawing every swarmling. The host updates the ones drawn farthest from their real position first, weighted by how close they are to the client (one at the client's feet is kept to within centimeters, one 60 m away to half a meter), and also updates each one now and then regardless. A swarmling that starts a lunge within reach of a player is updated immediately (the wind-up is the player's warning), and a new one is placed immediately. The same tracks are used to resolve the client's shots at the horde (TryShown(int, double, out Vector3, out float, out SwarmSurface), for lag compensation), so the client hits what it was shown. Doesn't allocate after the first few snapshots. api/LastFleet.Networking.Session.Arrival.summary: Class ArrivalJitter Namespace LastFleet.Networking.Session Assembly LastFleet.Networking.dll Measures how unevenly a client's commands reach the host, and from that how many commands should be kept waiting there. This is the jitter buffer. public sealed class ArrivalJitter Inheritance object ArrivalJitter Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Each input message's newest command was made one tick after the previous message's, so on a perfectly even link the host tick it arrives on minus its sequence number would be the same every time. How much that value moves from one message to the next is the jitter (the RFC 3550 estimator, in ticks). The client paces its clock to keep TargetWaiting commands buffered on the host. That's enough to cover nearly every late command, so the host rarely has to repeat the last one (which the client's prediction can't know about). It's also no more than the link needs, since each buffered command adds a tick of input delay. api/LastFleet.Physics.DebrisWorld.html.summary: Class DebrisWorld Namespace LastFleet.Physics Assembly LastFleet.Physics.dll Cosmetic debris. When a prop breaks, it bursts into box fragments that tumble and bounce off the level and each other under Jolt rigid-body physics, then disappear. public sealed class DebrisWorld : IDisposable Inheritance object DebrisWorld Implements IDisposable Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks This is a separate Jolt physics system from the simulation's JoltWorld, with its own copy of the level's boxes. Debris never affects gameplay, so it can run on the client, at frame rate, without determinism. It's stepped on its own worker thread, with collision spread over Jolt's thread pool. Begin(float) starts a step and returns right away, and Complete() waits for it and shows its fragments. Each frame completes the step started the frame before, draws it, then begins the next one. So the step runs alongside the rest of the frame and the pieces are drawn a frame late, which is fine since they're only for show. Every other method waits for any running step first, so it's safe to call at any time from the thread that owns the world. Constructors DebrisWorld(int) Creates the debris world and starts its worker thread. public DebrisWorld(int maxFragments = 160) Parameters maxFragments int The most fragments alive at once. When full, the oldest are removed first. That's what debris cost the calling thread, and it's close to zero when the step ran alongside the frame. public double WaitMilliseconds { get; } Property Value double WorkerThreads Number of Jolt worker threads for debris. It's the machine's core count minus two (the game's own thread and the debris thread), clamped between one and four. public static int WorkerThreads { get; } Property Value int Methods AddStaticMesh(MeshData, int) Adds the level for debris to land on. api/LastFleet.Physics.JoltWorld.html.summary: Class JoltWorld Namespace LastFleet.Physics Assembly LastFleet.Physics.dll The level's collision. Uses Jolt for characters moving through static geometry, and a triangle hierarchy for rays. public sealed class JoltWorld : ICollisionWorld, IDisposable Inheritance object JoltWorld Implements ICollisionWorld IDisposable Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Characters are Jolt virtual characters: kinematic capsules that slide along walls, walk up steps, stick to the floor going down slopes and stairs, and refuse slopes steeper than their limit. The simulation decides the velocity; this class only works out where that velocity takes the capsule. Static geometry becomes one Jolt box body per MeshPart, fitted exactly, including rotation. Ray casts run against the triangles themselves through TriangleRaycaster. Both were written around gaps in an earlier BRUTAL release's Jolt binding (no mesh shapes or ray queries, and a crash building convex hulls). The current one (2026.10.4) builds mesh, convex hull and cylinder shapes and casts rays against them: see AddStaticMeshBody(ReadOnlySpan<Vector3>, Vector3, Quaternion) and docs/plans/model-colliders.md. Everything runs on the calling thread, so the same inputs give the same results. Moving a character and casting rays don't allocate managed memory. api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Layouts.LayoutSolv.title: Class LayoutSolver | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Layouts.LayoutSolv.summary: Class LayoutSolver Namespace LastFleet.ProcGen.Layouts Assembly LastFleet.ProcGen.dll Places a mission graph's rooms on the grid, then adds loops and one-way shortcuts. public sealed class LayoutSolver Inheritance object LayoutSolver Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks First a backtracking search puts each room (with up to two corridors before it) at a free connector of its parent, with no overlaps. Then it adds loops between rooms that are far apart in the tree: directly, through a short straight corridor where two doorways face each other, or through a corridor routed around corners across empty cells (at most MaxRouteCells) between any two free doorways on a story. Loops never cross regions, so a loop can't get around a lock. Next it keeps adding loops until the fraction of rooms on a loop reaches what the recipe asks for (Share). Then it adds one-way shortcuts across the gates between zones, each opening only from the deeper zone's side (OneWayPerGate), so none of them gets around a lock either. A layout with fewer loops than the template asks for is thrown away and tried again. api/LastFleet.ProcGen.LevelGenerator.htm.title: Class LevelGenerator | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.ProcGen.LevelGenerator.htm.summary: Class LevelGenerator Namespace LastFleet.ProcGen Assembly LastFleet.ProcGen.dll Generates a level from a seed (design doc, "Procedural level generation"). Pass 1 builds the mission graph from the template, pass 2 lays out the biome's room modules, and pass 3 assembles the mesh and places the fight. The same seed, template and library always give the same level on every machine, so co-op peers only send the seed. public sealed class LevelGenerator Inheritance object LevelGenerator Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks A template can ask for rooms built from the seed (ParametricRoom), which are added to the library for that level only. Each deck also gets halls built in its theme (ParametricHall), offered alongside the kit's corridors on that deck. The station's fixtures (tanks, the reservoir, the airlock's fittings) are prop models from props, as the template names them. The designers' procgen data (data, or just the built-in tags if none is given) tags each room. Constructors LevelGenerator(ModuleLibrary, ModelLibrary, ProcGenData?) Generates a level from a seed (design doc, "Procedural level generation"). Pass 1 builds the mission graph from the template, pass 2 lays out the biome's room modules, and pass 3 assembles the mesh and places the fight. The same seed, template and library always give the same level on every machine, so co-op peers only send the seed. public LevelGenerator(ModuleLibrary library, ModelLibrary props, ProcGenData? data = null) Parameters library ModuleLibrary props ModelLibrary data ProcGenData Remarks A template can ask for rooms built from the seed (ParametricRoom), which are added to the library for that level only. Each deck also gets halls built in its theme (ParametricHall), offered alongside the kit's corridors on that deck. The station's fixtures (tanks, the reservoir, the airlock's fittings) are prop models from props, as the template names them. The designers' procgen data (data, or just the built-in tags if none is given) tags each room. Fields PlanAttempts How many seeds made from a plan level's own are tried when its mission can't be read into the level (PlanMissionException), before giving up. public const int PlanAttempts = 8 Field Value int RemakeAttempts How many times a level is regenerated when it can't place the reservoirs its template requires. public const int RemakeAttempts = 6 Field Value int Properties Data The designers' procgen data used to make levels, with its furniture models resolved from Props. public ProcGenData Data { get; } Property Value ProcGenData Library The kit of rooms that levels are laid out from (KitRooms). public ModuleLibrary Library { get; } Property Value ModuleLibrary Props The prop models the station's fixtures are made from. public ModelLibrary Props { get; } Property Value ModelLibrary Methods ForKit(ModelLibrary, ProcGenData, string) Creates a generator for biome's levels. Its kit of rooms is built from data's archetypes (KitRooms), and the station's fixtures come from props. public static LevelGenerator ForKit(ModelLibrary props, ProcGenData data, string biome = "station") Parameters props ModelLibrary data ProcGenData biome string Returns LevelGenerator Exceptions InvalidDataException A kit room can't be built. Generate(MissionTemplate, ulong) Generates the level for template from seed. public GeneratedLevel Generate(MissionTemplate template, ulong seed) Parameters template MissionTemplate seed ulong Returns GeneratedLevel Remarks If the template requires reservoirs and the level can't place the minimum it asks for, the level is regenerated from seeds derived from this one (the same on every machine), up to RemakeAttempts times. The attempt that places the most reservoirs is kept, and its Remade says how many retries it took. LayOut(MissionTemplate, ulong, ProcGenData) Builds the plan's level for template (Plan) from seed, with its mission read into it: the plan picked from the seed, then the level built from it, or from seeds made from it until the mission can be read in. Returns the level, the seed it was built from and how many tries came before it. public static (PlanLevel Level, ulong Seed, int Attempt) LayOut(MissionTemplate template, ulong seed, ProcGenData data) Parameters template MissionTemplate seed ulong data ProcGenData Returns (PlanLevel Level, ulong Seed, int Attempt) Exceptions PlanMissionException No try out of PlanAttempts could take the mission. Type(MissionTemplate, MissionGraph, ulong, ProcGenData) Types the rooms of template's level for seed (RoomTyper). It uses the archetypes the template names (two-story ones only if the level has two stories), and builds rooms from at most as many archetypes as the drawn count of built rooms (ParametricRooms). public static RoomTyping Type(MissionTemplate template, MissionGraph graph, ulong seed, ProcGenData data) Parameters template MissionTemplate graph MissionGraph seed ulong data ProcGenData Returns RoomTyping Exceptions RoomTypingException The rules can't all be met. Its trace says why.

It applies to a corner of the outline where the room is on one side only and neither of the two walls meeting there has a doorway. The cut runs Size meters along each wall from where their inner faces meet. It's built as a solid wedge in the corner: a box rotated 45°, since that's the only solid level collision supports besides an axis-aligned box. Its face is the cut and the rest sits inside the walls. api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Doors.DoorK.summary: Enum DoorKind Namespace LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Doors Assembly LastFleet.ProcGen.dll What kind of door a shut door is, which sets how it looks. Each kind is recognizable from across a room. public enum DoorKind : byte Fields Keycard = 0 A deck gate, opened by its keycard. Grey leaves with a red band and a keycard reader beside it. Lockdown = 1 The gate into the last deck, sealed until the hack is done. Leaves striped yellow and black. OneWay = 2 A one-way shortcut back across a gate. From the side it doesn't open from, its leaves show a no-entry sign. From the side it does open from, it has a green band and a release panel beside it. Closet = 3 A spawn closet door that reinforcements come out of. Plain grey with a hazard kick plate. Airlock = 4 The airlock's inner door, which opens once the lock has cycled. A heavy door in hazard paint. Pressure = 5 A pressure door through a bulkhead, open until its compartment seals (BulkheadDoor). Grey leaves with a red seal band across them at the height of a hand and a white stripe under it. Auto = 6 A room's door onto a hall (RoomDoorSpot) that slides open for whoever comes near and shuts behind them. Grey leaves with a lit strip across them and a dark window above. Interact = 7 A room's door onto a hall that someone has to open (or shut) by hand: a player with Interact, a soldier on his way through; the swarm batters it open. Grey leaves with a handle at the seam and a kick plate.

api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Dressing.St.summary: Class StationDressing Namespace LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Dressing Assembly LastFleet.ProcGen.dll Dresses the placed rooms so they look like a space station instead of boxes under the sky: a ceiling over every room (where no room is above it), light panels in the ceiling, and the lights they cast, colored by the room's role. A few panels are dead and a few flicker. public static class StationDressing Inheritance object StationDressing Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks A ceiling is a one-sided face pointing down. Rays from below (shots, grenades, a character's head) hit it. A ray from above passes through, like any face seen from inside, so the navigation grid, which looks down each column for floors, never mistakes a roof for a floor. A lit panel is its own breakable glass part (LightPrefix). Shots and blasts break it and its light goes out, leaving the dark housing. Rays only hit its underside and sides, and nothing else collides with panels, so they cost the physics nothing. api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Supplies.St.summary: Class StationReservoirs Namespace LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Supplies Assembly LastFleet.ProcGen.dll Deep reservoirs (the template's ReservoirSettings). A reservoir is a big tank in a room further from the airlock's port than a hose reaches, plus an outlet on a wall near the airlock. The two are joined by the reservoir feed (LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Supplies.ReservoirFeed, a network routed along the walls and ceilings), with one valve at the reservoir and some along the way (ValveSpot). In game terms it's a TankSpot at the outlet: players take the hose there once every valve is open, and the gauge there shows the reservoir's level. Reservoirs are placed after everything else in the level (tanks, containers, cargo), using their own random stream, so they don't change anything else a seed produces. The reservoir, outlet and valves use the template's models (LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Dressing.StationProp). public static class StationReservoirs Inheritance object StationReservoirs Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Fields PipeHeight How high above the floor the pipe leaves the reservoir, in meters. api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.html.title: Namespace LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.html.summary: Namespace LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels Namespaces LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Airlocks LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Doors LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Dressing LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Hull LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Lights LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Pods LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Supplies LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Warship Classes Decks A station's decks. Each deck is a zone behind a keycard gate (a room's region). Gives each deck's name and color, which its room baseboards, gate bulkheads and signs, and the HUD use, so you always know which deck you're on and which one you're heading into. LevelAssembler Pass 3 (design doc): turns the placed modules into one level mesh (with unused doorways walled up and locked doors in place) and populates it. That means player spawns from the insertion, soldier squads from the rooms' spawn points within the template's soldier budget, weapons, the objective and extraction. After that come the props the placement rules put in the rooms (LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Dressing.StationPlacements): keycards, ammo crates, containers, cargo, supplies and tanks. MissionLayout The mission's key points in a generated level: where the team arrives, the keys and locks, the objective, the extraction point, the spawn closets, and fallback reinforcement spawns (just inside the arena's doorways, facing in) for layouts with no closet by the arena. Also the weapons and supplies lying around, the containers to search, the cargo to carry out, the tanks to pump into the dropship, and the hull breaches the horde can come through. PatrolRoom A room patrols can come out of when no spawn closet will do (docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 14): one the recipe's threat names a source (a security office, crew quarters), with the spots soldiers start from in it. RoomRects Splits a placed room's ground story into rectangles of whole cells that cover it exactly once. A rectangular room is just its own bounds; an L becomes two. Anything laid out on a grid across a room (ceiling panels, the ceiling body) is laid out on each rectangle. Structs CornerChamfer A room corner cut at 45° (Chamfer). It applies to a corner of the outline where the room is on one side only and neither of the two walls meeting there has a doorway. The cut runs Size meters along each wall from where their inner faces meet. It's built as a solid wedge in the corner: a box rotated 45°, since that's the only solid level collision supports besides an axis-aligned box. Its face is the cut and the rest sits inside the walls. Anything that runs along the walls (trims, a duct, lockers) stops short of it (WallRun). PartRooms The room a level part belongs to, or the two rooms a doorway's part (a lintel, a locked door) sits between, so the client can skip drawing parts of rooms it cannot see. -1 for none: such a part is always drawn. WallRun A straight stretch of a placed room's walls on its ground story, used by the dressing to run things along it (trims, ducts, pipes). Holds which way it faces out of the room, where it runs (in meters, along X for a north or south wall, along Z for an east or west one), where its inner face is on the cross axis, and which way is into the room (+1 or -1).

It stays shut until someone stands at it on the deeper zone's side, and it only opens from there. So it never lets the squad past a gate before they have its keycard. It only gives them a short way back once they're through (OpensFrom). Constructors LoopRules(int, int, float, (int Min, int Max), float) How a level's loops get made, beyond how many each zone gets (Loops). api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Missions.html.title: Namespace LastFleet.ProcGen.Missions | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Missions.html.summary: Namespace LastFleet.ProcGen.Missions Classes AirlockModels The models of the airlock's fittings in the hull (a mission template's "airlock"): the dropship's intake, where a tank's hose couples, and its cargo chute, each a station prop ("file/Object"). AlertSettings How a mission's station alert level builds up (its template's "alert"): how it rises over time and with noise, how little it drops, and what it does to patrols and the horde. The fight's Director reads these (see its AlertTuning). BoardingTargets Where a boarding action's targets are in a ship (design doc, "Boarding action: a ship in the fight"): its gun batteries, its reactor and its fire suppression controls. Read the same from the level on every machine, so the host's mission and everyone's markers agree. BreachRule How a plan mission's breaches go (docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 10; the breaches block of a template's plan): the chance a breach seals its compartment for good when the mission can still be finished without it, and the districts never lost, whose compartments only ever seal for a while. How tough windows are, the pull and the timers are every mission's (breaches.json). EarlyExtractionSettings Settings for leaving early on the docked dropship (a mission template's "earlyExtraction"): whether the squad can, how long they hold at the airlock to leave, and what the fleet needs to get for it to count as a success. That requisition is the supplies running short, topped up to ReserveJumps jumps of reserve, with some minimum amount either way. ExitRule How a plan mission's squad gets on or off: the kinds of exit it would rather use, in order. The first kind the level has wins. FleetRule The fleet seen from a plan's windows (docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 10): how many ships hang in space round the level, and how far off, set in the mission template's plan (fleet). GenerationSettings The settings a lobby can change on a mission template before a level is generated: how many decks, how many soldiers, how much loot, how many stories, and how many rooms are built from the seed. They're encoded in the level's name (Encode()), so every co-op peer generates the same level from the name alone. KeycardRule Where a plan mission's keycards go: one for each gate the hack doesn't open, in a room of the zone before its gate, off the way through. KeycardStep The keycard for each deck's gate into the next (but the gate the hack opens), on a branch off the deck's way through, sometimes behind a room to explore: before its lock, so the level can always be finished. On every deck. LevelRecipe How a level's mission graph is grown, deck by deck (MissionGraph). It's a list of steps in order: first the main path (MainPathStep), then the keycard (KeycardStep), then any side and loot rooms. Every step is applied to each deck in turn, so the level is always finishable by construction: each keycard sits on its deck before the gate it opens. This is a mission template's recipe. A template without one grows from its room counts (Of(MissionTemplate)). LoopRules How a level's loops get made, beyond how many each zone gets (Loops). Sets how far apart in the room tree a loop's two ends have to be, how long a corridor routed around corners for a loop can be, what fraction of rooms should end up on a loop, the most that should be dead ends, and how many one-way shortcuts cross each gate between zones. Loops keep getting added until both the loop and dead-end targets are met, or no more fit. LootRoomsStep Loot rooms, each off any room of the deck but its ends (and other loot rooms). LootSettings Weapon loot settings for a mission's level (design doc, "Procedural weapons and loot"). Loot tables are only named here, not loaded; the game rolls them. Item level goes up by one per zone, so deeper decks have better weapons. Loot rooms hold caches. On top of that, the Director hides a few stashes in each zone, placed to reward going out of the way or taking on a guarded room. MainPathStep Builds the main path through each deck: the first room (the insertion, or a transit set piece behind the gate), some rooms along the way, then the objective and arena on the second-to-last deck and extraction at the end of the last. It's always the recipe's first step and runs on every deck. MissionGraph Pass 1 (design doc): the mission as a tree of rooms starting from the insertion, with key and lock pairs. It's grown by the template's recipe (LevelRecipe), applying each step in turn on each deck, so it's always completable by construction: each keycard sits off the path before its lock. MissionTemplate A mission template (design doc, "Mission types" and "Pass 1: mission graph"), read from content/defs/missions/*.json. It sets how many rooms of each kind, how many key and lock pairs, loops and soldiers, and how many stories the level can climb through (1 keeps it flat). ObjectiveRule What a plan mission's squad comes for and where it is: a room of the zone before the last (docs/plans/structure- first.md, "Objective kinds"). Whatever its kind, finishing it opens the gate into the last zone, where extraction is. PlanRecipe How a mission reads itself into a plan's level (docs/plans/structure-first.md, "The mission recipe"). The level's structure is built first, so there's nothing to grow: these are rules for choosing among the rooms it has. PodRule A plan mission's escape pods: bays on the hull, each with a pod or two, that take one or two players off at any time (never a crate). Whoever gets off by whatever way, the squad ends up together. RecipeStep One step of a level's recipe (LevelRecipe): what it adds to each deck's rooms, in the recipe's order. ReservoirSettings Settings for deep reservoirs of fuel or water (a mission template's "reservoir"). A reservoir is a big tank deeper in the station than a hose can reach. RoomRule Which of a plan's rooms a mission rule is after: those with any of Any's tags, from their archetype (archetypes.json), a tag also matching every tag under it (room.storage takes room.storage.armory). With no tags, every room. SideRoomsStep Adds side rooms to explore. Each is a dead end off the deck's main path, sometimes two rooms deep. A one-deck level gets none. StationSupplies The supplies a station's cargo can hold, as defined in the game's data (the loot data's fleet supplies, put into use with Use(StationSupplies?); with no data, Shipped). Lists every supply a station can be chosen for (a CargoFocus), each with its color, used for a tank's band and glow when it holds that supply. Which ones are kept in tanks is up to the mission template (TankSupplies). Every co-op peer generates its levels from the same set. TankKind A kind of supply tank a station's rooms can have (a mission template's "tankKinds"). It sets the model (a station prop in content/props, LastFleet.ProcGen.Levels.Dressing.StationProps), how much room it takes, which supplies it can hold, and how often it's picked over other kinds that can hold the same supply. ThreatRule How hard a plan mission's places are defended, and what that sets (docs/plans/structure-first.md, "Threat drives the fight"; the threat block of a template's plan). Each zone's threat rises from the first to the last, scaled by its district and by what a room is (a security office more, quarters less). While the squad is somewhere, its threat sets how often the Director sends a patrol and how big; the station's alert speeds both on top. api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Modules.AngledHall.title: Class AngledHall | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Modules.AngledHall.summary: Class AngledHall Namespace LastFleet.ProcGen.Modules Assembly LastFleet.ProcGen.dll Builds a stretch of ring hall smooth (docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 7): its cells are still the grid's, but its walls follow its band (HallBand: round a ring's bend, or straight on a slant) as straight sides, each a box turned to its side, so the hall reads as a curve instead of steps. The rooms either side keep their walls on the grid. public static class AngledHall Inheritance object AngledHall Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks The floor covers every cell. The walls stand on the band's two edges, clipped to the stretch's own cells. Where a doorway's edge crosses the band (the next stretch, or a door through a bulkhead), the hall runs on through it, and a doorway narrower than the edge gets jambs along the edge either side of it so a shut door seals. Where a doorway is off the band (a room's door), a throat runs from it to the wall: two jambs along the way in, the wall cut between them. The space between the band and the cells' edges is shut in by the walls either side, so nobody sees or reaches it. Every wall is a box (BoxFit), so it collides as one; nothing is left to the dressing but its ceiling and lights (Band). The theme sets the size and openness: one to three cells wide, two to four long, one or two stories, and open across a wide end so two halls placed end to end read as one. The style sets the look (Hall): ribs, arches, columns or pillars along the hall; a floor of plain plate, a grated channel lit from below, or light strips along the walls and down the middle; and lighting along the bottom or top of the walls or on whatever stands along the hall (the lighting is in ParametricHall.Lights.cs). public static class ParametricHall Inheritance object ParametricHall Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks To the layout these are corridors, offered on their own deck alongside the kit's narrow corridors. They're read by ModuleReader like any other module, so they follow the kit's rules (whole cells, clear doorways). Anything hanging under the ceiling (a frame's beam, an arch's haunches) has no top face for rays, the same as the station's lintels, so the navigation grid never mistakes it for floor. It gets its own collision body to stop characters. Floor lights are render-only and flush with the floor. Generation is deterministic: the same seed, theme and style always give the same hall. Each one is built the same way a hand-made module would be, from boxes and markers, and read by ModuleReader. That way it follows the kit's rules (whole cells, clear doorways) and gets spawn spots found from its geometry the same way. public static class ParametricRoom Inheritance object ParametricRoom Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Furniture never blocks the way through. Every piece is tested on a half-meter grid of walkable floor, and only kept if every doorway can still reach every other with room to pass, and no open floor gets closed off behind it. api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Modules.html.title: Namespace LastFleet.ProcGen.Modules | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Modules.html.summary: Namespace LastFleet.ProcGen.Modules Classes AngledHall Builds a stretch of ring hall smooth (docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 7): its cells are still the grid's, but its walls follow its band (HallBand: round a ring's bend, or straight on a slant) as straight sides, each a box turned to its side, so the hall reads as a curve instead of steps. The rooms either side keep their walls on the grid. GltfNodes Reads the node tree of a .gltf or .glb file: names, transforms and custom properties, but not geometry. HallArc A hall bent round a center: a ring hall's corridor (HallBand), the band either side of a circle Radius out from Center. HallBand The floor plan of a hall built smooth rather than stepped on the grid (docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 7): a band HalfWidth either side of a middle line, on the ground (X and Z, in meters). A ring hall's middle line is a circle (HallArc), a bridge's on a slant a straight line (HallLine). Its walls are the band's edges cut into straight sides no longer than MostSide. HallLine A straight hall on a slant: a bridge running out from a ring station's core at any angle (HallBand), the band either side of the line from From to To, open at both ends. HallTheme A deck theme and how its halls are laid out (ParametricHall): width and length, how often they're two stories tall, how open they are, and the surface style that sets how they look. A mission template lists its themes (HallThemes, "hallThemes" in its file). If it doesn't, Defaults is used. KitRooms A biome's kit of rooms (Kit): the archetypes offered to every level in the biome. Each one is built once, seeded from its own id, so the kit is identical in every level and on every machine, just like the hand-made modules it replaced. Each becomes a module with its archetype's id and fills that archetype's roles: the insertion bay, the corridors and stairwell, the spawn closet, the keycard room, the objective and extraction rooms, and the rooms in between. ModuleLibrary A biome's room modules (its kit, KitRooms, plus the level's own), sorted by id so the order is stable. ModuleReader Turns a room's scene, as written by a built room or hall (ParametricRoom, ParametricHall), into a RoomModule. It also checks the scene against the kit's rules, so a mistake is reported by name when the room is built instead of showing up as a broken level. ParametricHall Procedurally built halls for a deck's theme (HallTheme) in its surface style (SurfaceStyle). The theme sets the size and openness: one to three cells wide, two to four long, one or two stories, and open across a wide end so two halls placed end to end read as one. The style sets the look (Hall): ribs, arches, columns or pillars along the hall; a floor of plain plate, a grated channel lit from below, or light strips along the walls and down the middle; and lighting along the bottom or top of the walls or on whatever stands along the hall (the lighting is in ParametricHall.Lights.cs). ParametricRoom Procedurally built rooms, as opposed to hand-made ones: a footprint of any size and shape (a rectangle, or an L, a U, or a cross from a shape recipe), doorways on every side, and furniture laid out in one of a few styles (offices, a warehouse, a lab, a plaza), all from a seed. Each one is built the same way a hand-made module would be, from boxes and markers, and read by ModuleReader. That way it follows the kit's rules (whole cells, clear doorways) and gets spawn spots found from its geometry the same way. RoomFinish The finishing details of a built room (ParametricRoom) beyond its footprint: its surface style, its furnishing, how much its corners are cut, and whether pillars hold up its ceiling. RoomModule A room that levels are laid out from. It's either built from an archetype (ParametricRoom) or a hall, and checked against the kit's rules by ModuleReader. It holds the geometry, the footprint in grid cells, the connectors, the roles it can fill (tags), and markers in module coordinates. SceneNode A node in a glTF scene: its name, world transform, whether it has a mesh, and its custom properties. ShipBay A hangar's ship entrance (docs/plans/structure-first.md, hangars): its wall on the hull left open the room's full height, but for a post at each end, behind a field that keeps the air in and people from walking out (shots and the view go through it). A dropship comes in through it to its pad, so the lane from it in is kept clear of anything placed (KeepClear). In the room's own frame. Structs ModuleConnector A doorway on a module's footprint, at the middle of cell Cell along Side, on story Level of the module (0 for the ground floor, 1 for one story up). The opening is Width wide and centered Shift along the side from the cell's middle. That covers both a standard 2 m kit doorway and a wide hall's fully open end. Where two openings of different widths meet, the level walls up whatever part doesn't face the other opening (LevelAssembler). ModuleLight An extra light that comes with a module, on top of the ceiling panels (for example a glow under a floor grate or along a trim strip), in module coordinates. Like the panel lights, it only lights its own room. If it has half axes it's a rect light: the glowing surface itself, shining toward the side the cross product of its axes points to (PointLight.Rect).

api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Networks.LaneGraph.summary: Class LaneGraph Namespace LastFleet.ProcGen.Networks Assembly LastFleet.ProcGen.dll The graph of places a level's networks can run (LaneKind). That covers a band along every room's walls above the doorway lintels, a higher lane along them (under the ceiling, or up a tall room's wall), a standoff lane offset from the wall to get past whatever already runs along it, straight spans across open ceilings from wall to wall, risers between these and up tall rooms' walls, crossings through walls and floors rooms share (including next to a doorway) and through doorway lintels, and the empty cells enclosed by rooms (service cells). public sealed class LaneGraph Inheritance object LaneGraph Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Each lane is a straight edge between two nodes along one of the level's axes. A lane with a fitting in it (ILaneObstacles) is dropped, and a lane along a wall that's blocked by the room's own structure (a hall's rib) becomes a crossing through it. Nodes and edges are numbered in the order they're found (room by room, story by story, cell by cell, side by side, then the service cells and the floors). That order is the same on every machine, and the router breaks ties using those numbers. No lane crosses a doorway's opening (every lane goes over its lintel or through it, and none goes up a wall where there's a doorway), a hull wall (only walls between two rooms, or between a room and a service cell, are crossed), or the space reserved for standing and props (every horizontal lane is above BandHeight, higher than any prop). api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Networks.LaneKind..title: Enum LaneKind | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Networks.LaneKind..summary: Enum LaneKind Namespace LastFleet.ProcGen.Networks Assembly LastFleet.ProcGen.dll What a lane in a LaneGraph runs along or through. Each kind is priced by a network's NetworkCosts. Every lane is straight, either horizontal or vertical, along one of the level's axes. public enum LaneKind Fields Wall = 0 Along a wall at BandHeight, the band just above the doorway lintels. Also used for lanes higher up a tall room's wall. OverDoorway = 1 Along a wall at band height, over a doorway, against its lintel. CeilingEdge = 2 Along a wall right under the ceiling, at CeilingEdgeHeight. On a tall room's wall, where more of the room is above that height, the lane is Wall instead. Standoff = 3 Along a wall at ceiling-edge height, offset from it (StandoffInset) to get past whatever already runs along the wall (a duct, a room's pipes). Also the short hop out to it from the wall. OpenCeiling = 4 Straight across a room under its ceiling, from one wall to the opposite wall. Riser = 5 Straight up a wall: from the band to the lane above it, or up one story on a tall room's wall. ThroughWall = 6 Through a wall shared by two rooms, at ceiling-edge height; up through the floor between two stacked rooms; or through part of a room's own structure that's in the way of a lane along a wall (a hall's rib, a column). ThroughLintel = 7 Through the lintel over a doorway from one room into the next, at ceiling-edge height. Service = 8 Through an empty cell enclosed by rooms (a service cell). The route seals it as a duct.

api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Networks.NetworkRo.summary: Class NetworkRouter Namespace LastFleet.ProcGen.Networks Assembly LastFleet.ProcGen.dll Finds a network's cheapest route through a level's lanes (LaneGraph) using A*. Costs are integers (NetworkCosts) and ties are broken by node index, so every machine finds the same route. public static class NetworkRouter Inheritance object NetworkRouter Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks A lane costs the network's price for its kind, either per centimeter (rounded) or once for a wall or lintel crossing, plus Bend wherever the route turns. An open-ceiling span longer than OpenSpan is never used, and neither is a lane already used by a different kind of network (LaneUsage). A lane already used by the same kind costs a quarter less, so same-kind networks bundle together. If the route goes through more service cells than ServiceCells, it's searched again with service cells disabled. The heuristic is the axis-aligned (Manhattan) distance to the goal, since every lane runs along an axis, times the cheapest per-centimeter cost of any lane. That never overestimates the real cost, so the route found is the cheapest. Methods Alternative(LaneGraph, NetworkSpec, NetworkRoute, IReadOnlyList<int>, LaneUsage?) A piece of furniture can stand in for it (Marker): when a built room's furnishing places that piece, it marks the spot where it stands, the same way a marker in a hand-made module does. public enum MissionMarker Fields None = 0 No marker. Terminal = 1 The objective terminal. It's hacked from in front. Extraction = 2 The extraction point, where the squad gets picked up. Key = 3 Where a keycard goes when no rule finds a place for it. Battery = 4 A warship's gun battery, sabotaged from in front (a boarding action). Reactor = 5 A ship's reactor, its power cut from in front of its console (a boarding action). Suppression = 6 A warship's fire suppression controls, repaired from in front (a boarding action).

api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Props.Prop.title: Enum PropKind | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Props.Prop.summary: Enum PropKind Namespace LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Props Assembly LastFleet.ProcGen.dll What a prop is in gameplay terms, which decides what placing it creates. Furniture is built into the room. A footlocker, case, cargo crate, supply pile, keycard, ammo crate or tank is a mission object. public enum PropKind : byte Fields Furniture = 0 A piece of furniture built into the room: a solid box, possibly breakable. Items can sit on top of a low one. Footlocker = 1 A footlocker to search. Its body is built into the level against a wall, and is solid. Case = 2 A supply case to search, sitting on top of something. Cargo = 3 A big crate of fleet supplies, carried out with both hands. Supplies = 4 A pile of supplies, rolled from the mission's pile table. Keycard = 5 A keycard for a locked gate. One per gate, placed in the rooms on the near side of the lock. Ammo = 6 An ammo crate. Tank = 7 A supply tank of the kinds the mission template uses. The template sets how many, and each must be within reach of its hose. Window = 8 A window onto space, on a wall on the hull: a frame in its color round a pane that shows the sector's sky, its glass from its sill up to its top. Built into the wall's face, it stands in nobody's way.

api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Rules.Plac.title: Enum PlacementAnchor | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Rules.Plac.summary: Enum PlacementAnchor Namespace LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Rules Assembly LastFleet.ProcGen.dll Where in a room a rule looks for spots to put its props. public enum PlacementAnchor : byte Fields Floor = 0 Anywhere on open floor. Random spots on the half-meter grid are tried, rotated 90 degrees or not. Wall = 1 Back against a wall, facing into the room. Tried every half meter along every stretch of wall. WallRun = 2 Back against a wall, centered on a stretch of wall that's long enough for the prop and its clear space. Corner = 3 In a corner, with its back against one wall and its side against the other. Center = 4 As close to the center of the room as it fits. NearDoor = 5 Against the wall next to a doorway, just clear of the opening, facing into the room. OnTop = 6 On top of something: the item spots marked in the room's module, and low furniture placed in the room. Ceiling = 7 Hanging from the ceiling, with its top against it. Hull = 8 Back against a wall on the hull (a plan's level: space past it), facing into the room, tried every half meter along the stretches of wall that are wholly on it. Where windows go.

api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Rules.Plac.title: Enum PlacementSkip | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Rules.Plac.summary: Enum PlacementSkip Namespace LastFleet.ProcGen.Placing.Rules Assembly LastFleet.ProcGen.dll Why a spot a rule tried for a prop was rejected. public enum PlacementSkip : byte Fields NoPlace = 0 The anchor found no spot anywhere in the room (no wall long enough, nothing to put it on). OutsideRoom = 1 It would stick partly outside the room's floor. TooTall = 2 It's taller than the space under the room's ceiling, ducts and lights. InTheWay = 3 Part of the room itself is in the way. TooClose = 4 Another prop is inside its clear space. Spacing = 5 Another prop from the same rule is closer than the rule's spacing. Taken = 6 A mission object is inside its clear space: a spawn, a weapon, a soldier. InALane = 7 It would sit in a lane that has to stay open: in front of a doorway or the stairs, or where something is used from. CutsOff = 8 It would cut one entrance to the room off from another, or close off open floor. CannotUse = 9 The floor in front of it, where it's used from, isn't open or can't be reached. Mission = 10 A mission-specific condition fails there (for example, a tank out of its hose's reach).

api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.MissionEmbed.title: Class MissionEmbedder | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.MissionEmbed.summary: Class MissionEmbedder Namespace LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans Assembly LastFleet.ProcGen.dll Reads a mission into a plan's level before its rooms are built (docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 4), by the template's recipe (PlanRecipe). The structure is already there, so nothing is grown: the embedder picks among the rooms the level has. public static class MissionEmbedder Inheritance object MissionEmbedder Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks The insertion is an airlock's vestibule (Vestibules(PlanLevel)) in a section at one end of the level, or the one nearest the plan's boarding pin (PlanPin), numbered first. Zones are runs counted out from it by the fewest bulkheads crossed to get somewhere, so every way from one zone into the next is a door or hatch through a bulkhead, and each of those is a gate (its lock the deeper zone's number). The objective is in the zone before the last and its hack opens the gate into the last, where extraction is, at the deepest exit the recipe allows. Every other gate's keycard is in a room of the zone before it, off the way through by as many doors as the recipe asks. That makes the mission finishable by construction: everywhere in a zone is reached from the insertion through zones no deeper, so each keycard is reachable with the keycards before it, and the hack's room is reachable with them all. Spawn closets go in void cells beside the halls, a few in each zone. Fields ClosetArchetype The archetype a spawn closet is built from (archetypes.json). public const string ClosetArchetype = "spawn_closet" Field Value string DamageControlArchetype The archetype a warship's fire suppression room is made into: damage control. public const string DamageControlArchetype = "damage_control" Field Value string EngineRoomArchetype The archetype a warship's reactor room is made into when it has no reactor or engine room. public const string EngineRoomArchetype = "engine_room" Field Value string GunDeckArchetype The archetype a warship's battery room is made into (archetypes.json): a gun deck, its shells racked. public const string GunDeckArchetype = "gun_deck" Field Value string VestibuleArchetype The archetype an airlock's vestibule is built from (archetypes.json), for its lockers and crates. public const string VestibuleArchetype = "insertion_bay" Field Value string

api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.PlanLevel.ht.title: Class PlanLevel | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.PlanLevel.ht.summary: Class PlanLevel Namespace LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans Assembly LastFleet.ProcGen.dll A plan's level for a seed, built from the outside in: its structure (PlanStructure), then the space its halls leave cut into rooms from each section's district program, then every room's doors, then every piece built as a room module and placed on the grid. public sealed class PlanLevel Inheritance object PlanLevel Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Plots are the cells between halls, in one section. Each is cut across its length into strips, so the rooms' walls line up along the hall, each strip a room picked by weight from its district (DistrictProgram), and the section's biggest plot holds its anchor. A strip deeper than MostDepth becomes a room in front and one behind; anything smaller than LeastRoom cells is left as void inside the hull. Each room's door faces the hall it has the most frontage on. A room between two halls usually gets a second door onto the other if it's shared (a mess, a lab), rarely if it's private (a cabin, a store). A room with no hall of its own gets a suite door through the room in front of it. Halls are built in stretches at most 8 cells each way, joined by openings as wide as the hall; pressure doors and hatches come from the structure. Every piece's doors are known before it's built, so no room has a doorway nothing uses. Identical pieces (a row of cabins, a stretch of corridor) are built once: a piece's seed comes from its archetype, shape and doors, and built pieces are kept for each set of procgen data. api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.html.title: Namespace LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans.html.summary: Namespace LastFleet.ProcGen.Plans Classes ArmPart A straight run of cells out from a point: a station's arm, a ring station's bridge, a docking boom. It grows from its At in its direction for a length picked from its range, as wide as its width either side of its line, so it stays on its line however long it's drawn. BoxModule A rectangle of cells: a station's hub or arm, a ship's sponson, a module bolted on. Its size is picked from its ranges; it can be mirrored across the centerline (a pair of sponsons from one part). BridgePart A straight run out from a center at any angle: a ring station's bridge from its core to its ring, on a slant as often as not (docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 7). It covers every cell its band (Width cells across) touches, from Span's first count of cells out from the center's middle to its second, so a hall laid on it runs smooth along its line (HallLine) rather than stepped on the grid. CrossHall A hall straight across a part, at a share of its length: a cross passage joining a ship's passageways, a hub's corridor across it. It reaches Reach cells either side of the part's line, or as far as the envelope allows with Inset cells to spare. DistrictPaint Cells a designer painted with one of a plan's districts (Paint), as rows of text the way a mask is (PaintedMask): # for a painted cell, anything else for none. The first row is the one with the least Z, and each row's first character the cell with the least X. DistrictProgram What a district is made of (districts.json): its anchor, the set piece its section is built round (a mess, a cargo hold, the bridge), and the rooms that fill the rest of its plots. DistrictRoom A kind of room a district is made of (DistrictProgram): the archetype it's built from (its style, furnishing and tags; its shape comes from the plot it's cut from), how many cells along its hall it takes, how often it's picked, whether it comes in a row of the same, and whether it's somewhere you go into rather than through. Envelope The outline of a level on one deck: the grid cells inside its hull, built from a plan's parts for a seed. Everything later in the structure-first pipeline (halls, sections, rooms) happens inside it, and its hull edges are where the level meets space. ExitPlanner Finds a plan level's ways on and off (docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 4): airlock vestibules, small rooms on the hull that open only onto a corridor, so the squad boards into a hallway rather than a store; and rooms on the hull for the squad to be taken off from. FillHall A hall that is the whole of the part it's laid on: every cell of it inside the envelope, whatever its shape. A mask painted as a hallway, a box made a concourse, an arm that is all corridor. HallPart One of a plan's halls, carved after the envelope and before any room. A hall is laid on one of the plan's parts (On) and follows the shape that part was drawn at (PartShape), so it fits however long or wide the part came out. Halls are carved in order; corridors first, then service ways round them. HullProfile A ship's hull: a length and a beam picked from their ranges, and a profile saying how wide it is along its length. It's mirrored across its centerline, with the bow at its At and the stern toward +X. LevelPlan A kind of level, as a designer composed it in Studio from parts: a frigate, a carrier, a station of hub and spokes, a ring station. Its envelope is built from its parts in order (Build(LevelPlan, ulong, int)), each adding cells or cutting them out. Its halls are carved into the envelope next, then it's cut into sections (Build(LevelPlan, ulong, int)). MissionEmbedder Reads a mission into a plan's level before its rooms are built (docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 4), by the template's recipe (PlanRecipe). The structure is already there, so nothing is grown: the embedder picks among the rooms the level has. PaintedMask Cells a designer painted, as rows of text: # for a cell, anything else for none. The first row is the one with the least Z, and each row's first character the cell with the least X. PlanCore A plan's stair core: stairs from one deck up to the one above, at a fixed frame of the ship, so it's in the same place on every seed. It stands as near the frame as a stairwell fits, clear of the halls on both decks, its foot joined to a corridor on the lower deck and its landing to one on the upper by short passages where they don't touch. PlanDeck One deck of a plan (Decks): its name, and its sections' districts if not the plan's. PlanLevel A plan's level for a seed, built from the outside in: its structure (PlanStructure), then the space its halls leave cut into rooms from each section's district program, then every room's doors, then every piece built as a room module and placed on the grid. PlanMission The mission read into a plan's level (MissionEmbedder): each piece's zone and role, each doorway's lock, the way through, and the mission graph the rest of generation reads, in which each piece is the node of its own index. PlanMissionException A mission recipe can't be read into a plan's level for a seed: no room on the hull for an airlock, or too few sections for two zones. The generator tries a seed made from this one. PlanPart One part of a level's plan (LevelPlan). Each part covers some grid cells, picked from its own random stream within the ranges a designer gave, and adds them to the envelope or cuts them out of it. PlanPicture Draws a plan's structure from above as a picture, for checking a plan by eye outside Studio (Studio's --plan-png): its sections tinted, its halls (main corridors palest, service ways brown), its bulkheads in red, its pressure doors in yellow and hatches in orange, the hull's edges, the centerline, and a mark every five cells (20 m). The bow is to the left. PlanPiece One piece of a plan's level, built as one room module: a room cut from a plot, or a stretch of hall. Long halls are built in stretches at most 8 cells each way, joined by openings as wide as the hall. PlanPin A set piece a designer pinned to a plan (docs/plans/structure-first.md, Phase 11): a room of an archetype that goes here, or where the squad boards. Like a stair core (PlanCore), it's placed on a part, so it follows the part however long or wide a seed draws it: along a line (a hull, a box, an arm), as a share of its length and cells off its middle line; round a ring, as cells from its center at its fewest radius, grown with it. PlanStructure A plan's structure for a seed, before any room: its envelope, the halls carved into it, the sections bulkheads cut it into (each with its district), the pressure doors and hatches where halls cross bulkheads, and service stubs so every section a service way passes has a hatch onto a corridor. Also what's wrong with it, for Studio and the tests. RingHall A hall round a ring part: a ring station's ring corridor, the corridor round its core. It runs FromOutside cells in from the ring's outside, Across meters wide, walkable all the way round, built smooth round its bend (AngledHall) on every cell it touches. RingPart A ring of cells round a center: a ring station's outer ring, or a disc when it's as wide as its radius (a hub). A cell is in it when its middle is within the outer radius and beyond the inner one, worked out in whole numbers. RingSplit A ring part cut into sections by angle, when each part is its own section (ByParts): a bulkhead out from its center at each of Quarters, so a ring station's ring is several sections, each its own zone, rather than one. The first piece round from the first quarter keeps the part's own section; the others get sections of their own after every part's, with the part's district. SectionCuts Bulkheads across one of a plan's parts, at shares of its length: a ship cut bow to stern into sections. Every cell of the envelope takes the section of where it falls along that part's line. SectionPlan How a plan's envelope is cut into sections (the parts between bulkheads, which become zones), and what each one is: bulkheads across one part (Cuts), each part its own section (a station's hub, each arm, each bridge), or districts painted on the plan's cells (Paint). SpineHall A hall along a part's line: a ship's spine, a passageway either side of it, a station arm's corridor, a bridge. It runs from From to To of the part's length (shares that may go past 0 and 1 to reach into the parts beside it), at Offset cells across, and stops where the envelope ends or leaves fewer than Inset cells either side of it for rooms. Only its longest stretch is kept, so it never breaks in two. Structs ExitPoint A way on or off a plan's level: a room against the hull and the side of it the hull is on, or a hangar the dropship lands in. PartShape The shape a part was drawn at for a seed, so halls and sections can follow it however long or wide it came out: a line it runs along (from its origin, in its direction, for its length, with cells either side of it), or a ring's center, radius and width. PlanDock Where the dropship docks to take the squad off: one side of a cell of the extraction room, on the hull with no doorway in it, where the airlock's outer hatch goes. PlanDoor A door in a plan's structure, on one side of a cell. PlanDoorway A doorway between two pieces of a plan's level, on one side of a cell of the first. ProfilePoint A point on a hull's profile (HullProfile): how wide the hull is at a place along it. Enums HallTier What a hall is for, which says how wide it reads and what it joins. PartMode What a plan's part does to the envelope built so far. PlanDoorKind The doors a plan's structure puts in before any room: where halls cross bulkheads. PlanDoorwayKind What joins two pieces of a plan's level. PlanPieceKind What a piece of a plan's level is: a room, a stretch of corridor or of service way, a spawn closet or stairs. PlanPinKind What a plan's pin holds in place (PlanPin).

api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Rooms.html.summary: Namespace LastFleet.ProcGen.Rooms Classes Footprint The grid cells a room occupies (each CellSize square and one story tall), in the room's own coordinates: X along its width, Z along its depth, and Level for its stories starting at 0. A kit module's footprint is a rectangle. A room built from a shape recipe can be any connected shape (an L, a U, a cross). RoomArchetype A kind of room the generator builds from designer data (archetypes.json). It sets the room's shape, the content tags it carries (which placement rules match on), the mission roles it can play, the surface style it's built and dressed in, and how it's furnished. A mission template lists the archetypes its built rooms are picked from, each picked by its weight. ShapeBuilder Makes a room's footprint from a ShapeRecipe and a random stream: a rectangle, an L, a T, a U, a cross, a blob, or a designer's stamp as drawn. The result is one story, with every cell connected to the others through shared sides, and its bounds start at cell (0, 0). The same recipe and stream give the same shape on every machine. Shapes are always generated in one orientation; the layout rotates them. ShapeRecipe How a room's footprint is made (ShapeBuilder): its kind, how big its bounds can be, and how much of them it leaves out. api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Seeding.Generation.title: Enum GenerationStage | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Seeding.Generation.summary: Enum GenerationStage Namespace LastFleet.ProcGen.Seeding Assembly LastFleet.ProcGen.dll The stages of a level's generation. Each has its own random streams (Streams). public enum GenerationStage Fields Mission = 0 The mission graph: rooms, roles, keys and locks. Typing = 1 Picks which room archetype is used for each room in the mission graph. Layout = 2 Places the rooms' footprints on the grid, with their doorways and loops. Structure = 3 Works out the walls, floors, ceilings and so on from the rooms' footprints. Styles = 4 Builds the structure in its surface styles. Placement = 5 Places props by rule. Networks = 6 Routes pipes, ducts and conduits over walls and ceilings. Loot = 7 What there is to find, by room type and zone. Validation = 8 Checks and repairs. Envelope = 9 A plan's envelope: the cells inside its hull, one stream per part (structure-first levels). Circulation = 10 A plan's halls, sections, bulkheads and hatches (structure-first levels). Plots = 11 A plan's plots cut into rooms, and their doors (structure-first levels). Embedding = 12 A plan level's exits and mission: zones, gates, keycards, the objective and extraction (structure-first levels).

api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Structures.EdgeCla.title: Class EdgeClassifier | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Structures.EdgeCla.summary: Class EdgeClassifier Namespace LastFleet.ProcGen.Structures Assembly LastFleet.ProcGen.dll Works out a room's structure from its shape: the floor and ceiling, the walls as straight runs between corners (cut open at the doorways), the doorways, and the corners. Each is a StructureMarker in the room's own coordinates. Surface styles build geometry from them, so no wall ever has to be placed or rotated by hand. public static class EdgeClassifier Inheritance object EdgeClassifier Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Walls sit on the room's outline (the edge of its FineGrid) and face inward (OnWall(Vector3, Vector3)), and a style builds each one inward from there. Floors cover each column's lowest story and ceilings its highest, using as few rectangles as possible (Cover(FineGrid)), so a rectangular room gets one of each per story. The order is fixed: story by story, floors, then ceilings, then walls and doorways side by side (north, east, south, west) from each side's low end, then corners. Every decision is made on integer fine cells, so it's identical on every machine. Methods Classify(Footprint, IReadOnlyList<WallOpening>, int, TagRegistry) Returns the structure markers of room room, with shape footprint and openings at openings. public static IReadOnlyList<StructureMarker> Classify(Footprint footprint, IReadOnlyList<WallOpening> openings, int room, TagRegistry tags) Parameters footprint Footprint openings IReadOnlyList<WallOpening> room int tags TagRegistry Returns IReadOnlyList<StructureMarker> Exceptions ArgumentException An opening isn't on a single straight run of the outline on its story.

api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Structures.html.title: Namespace LastFleet.ProcGen.Structures | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Structures.html.summary: Namespace LastFleet.ProcGen.Structures Classes EdgeClassifier Works out a room's structure from its shape: the floor and ceiling, the walls as straight runs between corners (cut open at the doorways), the doorways, and the corners. Each is a StructureMarker in the room's own coordinates. Surface styles build geometry from them, so no wall ever has to be placed or rotated by hand. FineGrid One story of a room at CellSize resolution: which half-meter squares of its floor are inside the room. Shapes finer than the layout's 4 m grid (chamfered corners, insets, pillars) get carved out here, and walls, floors and ceilings are found from its edges. StructureMarker A piece of a room's structure, found from the room's shape: what it is, where it is, which way it faces, and how long it is. Surface styles build geometry from markers, and placement rules anchor props to them. Structs FineRect A block of fine cells (FineGrid), starting at (X, Z) and Width by Depth in size. MarkerFrame Where a piece of structure is and which way it faces: a point on its surface, the direction into the room (Inward), and the direction along it (Along). Walls get built and props get placed in this frame, so nothing generated ever has to be rotated by hand. WallOpening A gap in a room's wall: a doorway, or a hall's end open all across. Given as two points on the room's outline in its own coordinates (meters, X and Z), on one story; the wall runs between them are left open. Enums StructureMarkerKind What kind of structure piece a marker is, as found from the room's shape.

api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Typing.RoomTyper.h.title: Class RoomTyper | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.ProcGen.Typing.RoomTyper.h.summary: Class RoomTyper Namespace LastFleet.ProcGen.Typing Assembly LastFleet.ProcGen.dll Types the rooms of a mission (RoomTyping) before they're laid out. Each room becomes either one of the mission's archetypes or the kit's own, so the level's room mix follows the designers' rules (TypingRule). public static class RoomTyper Inheritance object RoomTyper Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks This is a constraint search over the mission graph, in the style of wave function collapse. Each room's domain starts as the types that can play its role. The insertion, keycard rooms, the objective, extraction and transit are pinned to the kit's own rooms, because they need the kit's markers. Every other room can be the kit's own or any archetype that plays its role, each weighted (the kit gets KitShare, and the archetypes split the rest by their weights). Rules then narrow the domains: An adjacency rule, or a distance rule's minimum, is kept arc consistent between each pair of rooms it constrains. A count rule rules out its rooms once its scope has hit the maximum, or forces them once only the minimum is still possible. A distance rule's maximum rules out an A room that has no possible B room close enough. Once the level's archetype budget is spent, no other archetype is picked. Then the room with the lowest entropy (ties broken by node id) gets a type picked by weight, and the rules narrow again. When a domain empties, the search backs up and tries the next type, within a step budget. Every contradiction hit is traced, so a rule set that can't be satisfied reports why instead of hanging. Fields BudgetReason The reason given when an archetype is ruled out because the level's archetype budget is spent. public const string BudgetReason = "(the level builds no more archetypes)" Field Value string DrawnReason The reason given when a type is ruled out because another one was picked. public const string DrawnReason = "(another was drawn)" Field Value string Kit The type name for a kit room, as used in Type. public const string Kit = "kit" Field Value string MostArchetypes The most archetypes one level can type rooms from. public const int MostArchetypes = 63 Field Value int MostTraced The most contradictions the trace keeps. public const int MostTraced = 20 Field Value int PinnedReason The reason given for why the insertion, keycard rooms, the objective, extraction and transit are kit rooms. public const string PinnedReason = "(pinned: the mission's markers are the kit's)" Field Value string RoleReason The reason given when an archetype is ruled out because it doesn't play the room's role. public const string RoleReason = "(does not play its role)" Field Value string StepBudget The most types tried in total before the search gives up. public const int StepBudget = 4000 Field Value int Methods Type(MissionGraph, IReadOnlyList<RoomArchetype>, int, TypingData, TagRegistry, DeterministicRandom) Types the rooms of graph from archetypes (the ones the mission can build) according to data, building rooms from at most budget of them, with rolls from random. public static RoomTyping Type(MissionGraph graph, IReadOnlyList<RoomArchetype> archetypes, int budget, TypingData data, TagRegistry tags, DeterministicRandom random) Parameters graph MissionGraph archetypes IReadOnlyList<RoomArchetype> budget int data TypingData tags TagRegistry random DeterministicRandom Returns RoomTyping Exceptions RoomTypingException No typing satisfies the rules (or none was found within the step budget). Its trace says why.

Uses the row-vector convention, like System.Numerics: clip = position * ViewProjection. public static class CameraMath Inheritance object CameraMath Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks The projection is reverse-Z with an infinite far plane: depth is 1 at the near plane and falls towards 0 at infinity, so a 32-bit float depth buffer keeps its precision far into the distance. Depth tests use Greater and the depth buffer clears to 0. Clip space has +Y up. The renderer flips the viewport (negative height) to match Vulkan's +Y-down framebuffer, which also keeps glTF's counter-clockwise front faces counter-clockwise. Fields NearPlane Near plane distance, in meters. Close enough for a weapon held up to the eye. public const float NearPlane = 0.05 Field Value float ViewModelFieldOfView Vertical field of view the weapon in your hands is drawn with, in radians. It's fixed, so a wide field of view doesn't stretch the gun and the aiming zoom doesn't make it swell. public const float ViewModelFieldOfView = 0.9075712 Field Value float Methods AngleToPixels(float, float, float) Returns how many pixels from the screen center, vertically, a direction angle radians off the view axis lands.
