rooms = null, ReadOnlySpan<ReflectionCapture> captures = default, ReadOnlySpan<PointLight> captureLights = default, ReadOnlySpan<IndexRange> captureRanges = default, ReadOnlySpan<FogVolume> fogVolumes = default, ReadOnlySpan<MeshVertex> debris = default) Parameters overlay ReadOnlySpan<OverlayVertex> 2D triangles drawn over the scene, at most MaxOverlayVertices. effects ReadOnlySpan<EffectVertex> World-space effect triangles, at most MaxEffectVertices. partTints ReadOnlySpan<Vector4> One tint per world-mesh part (see Parts). rgb is blended over the part by alpha. A negative alpha hides the part: Gone for a part that no longer exists (a broken prop, an opened door), which rays also pass through, and Unseen for a part that's just not drawn this frame (a room out of sight), which rays still hit. If the span is empty or shorter than the part list, the remaining parts aren't tinted. ui ImDrawDataPtr Dear ImGui's draw data for this frame (ImGui.GetDrawData() after ImGui.Render()), or default for none. dynamicWorld ReadOnlySpan<MeshVertex> World-space, flat-shaded triangles rebuilt every frame (characters, loot, props, hoses), lit like the level. At most MaxDynamicVertices vertices, three per triangle. viewModel ReadOnlySpan<MeshVertex> The weapon in your hands: world-space, flat-shaded triangles lit like the level, but drawn with their own projection (ViewModelFieldOfView) and always in front of the world. That way the gun doesn't stretch with the field of view or clip through a wall you're standing against. At most MaxViewModelVertices vertices. lights ReadOnlySpan<PointLight> Point lights for the level and characters (not the view model). shadows ReadOnlySpan<ShadowView> Shadow maps to draw for some of the lights. shadowRanges ReadOnlySpan<IndexRange> The level index ranges the shadow maps draw. swarm ReadOnlySpan<SwarmInstance> The horde: one animated body (SetSwarmModel(AnimatedModel, ReadOnlySpan<Vector3>)) drawn at each instance. The first swarmNear use the full body and the rest use the far one. At most MaxSwarmInstances. swarmNear int How many of swarm, from the start, are drawn with the full body. skinned ReadOnlySpan<SkinnedDraw> Skinned bodies (soldiers and players on a rig). Each one is a mesh (AddSkinnedMesh(ReadOnlySpan<SkinnedVertex>)) skinned by its range of skinMatrices, lit like the level and casting shadows. skinMatrices ReadOnlySpan<Matrix4x4> Every skinned body's joint matrices this frame (each combines the joint's inverse bind, its pose and the body's world placement: Skin(in Matrix4x4, Span<Matrix4x4>)), at most MaxSkinMatrices. viewModelInWorld bool Whether viewModel is drawn with the world's projection instead of its own. This is used when the viewer's own body holds it (a Near draw), so the hands and the gun line up. rooms RoomLighting The level's rooms and their bounce light this frame (RoomLighting). Null for a level with no rooms, where the fill light comes from the sky only. captures ReadOnlySpan<ReflectionCapture> Rooms in rooms whose reflections need recapturing (ReflectionCapture). That's every room when a level starts, then only rooms whose lights have changed. captureLights ReadOnlySpan<PointLight> The lights for captures, a range per capture. captureRanges ReadOnlySpan<IndexRange> The level index ranges captures draw, a range per capture. fogVolumes ReadOnlySpan<FogVolume> Smoke in the air this frame (blasts, breaches), at most MaxFogVolumes. The atmosphere's froxel grid adds it to the level's haze. debris ReadOnlySpan<MeshVertex> Tumbling pieces of broken props: world-space, flat-shaded triangles like dynamicWorld, drawn and casting shadow map shadows the same way. They're kept out of the ray tracing scene, so a burst of them doesn't mean rebuilding a ray structure every frame. They have a budget of their own (MaxDebrisVertices), so a full dynamicWorld never leaves them out. Fields Gone Part tint alpha for a part that no longer exists (a broken prop, an opened door). It's neither drawn nor hit by rays. public const float Gone = -1 Field Value float Unseen Part tint alpha for a part that's just not drawn this frame (out of sight). Rays still hit it, because things out of sight still cast shadows into what you can see. public const float Unseen = -2 Field Value float Properties CaptureLights The lights used for the Captures. public ReadOnlySpan<PointLight> CaptureLights { get; } Property Value ReadOnlySpan<PointLight> CaptureRanges The level index ranges the Captures draw. public ReadOnlySpan<IndexRange> CaptureRanges { get; } Property Value ReadOnlySpan<IndexRange> Captures The rooms whose reflections should be recaptured this frame. public ReadOnlySpan<ReflectionCapture> Captures { get; } Property Value ReadOnlySpan<ReflectionCapture> Debris Pieces of broken props. Put the nearest first, because any past the limit are dropped. public ReadOnlySpan<PointLight> Lights { get; } Property Value ReadOnlySpan<PointLight> Overlay 2D triangles drawn last, over everything. public ReadOnlySpan<OverlayVertex> Overlay { get; } Property Value ReadOnlySpan<OverlayVertex> PartTints One tint per world-mesh part. public ReadOnlySpan<Vector4> PartTints { get; } Property Value ReadOnlySpan<Vector4> PreviousSkinMatrices The same bodies' joint matrices last frame, index for index with SkinMatrices, for the path tracer's motion vectors (a moving body's own motion, not only the camera's). A light uses map k when its Shadow is k. public ReadOnlySpan<ShadowView> Shadows { get; } Property Value ReadOnlySpan<ShadowView> SkinMatrices The joint matrices for Skinned. public ReadOnlySpan<Matrix4x4> SkinMatrices { get; } Property Value ReadOnlySpan<Matrix4x4> Skinned The skinned bodies this frame. public ReadOnlySpan<SkinnedDraw> Skinned { get; } Property Value ReadOnlySpan<SkinnedDraw> Swarm The horde's bodies this frame, near ones first. public ReadOnlySpan<SwarmInstance> Swarm { get; } Property Value ReadOnlySpan<SwarmInstance> SwarmNear How many of Swarm are near (drawn with the full body). public int SwarmNear { get; } Property Value int Ui Textured UI drawn over everything, including the overlay. public ImDrawDataPtr Ui { get; } Property Value ImDrawDataPtr ViewModel The weapon in your hands, drawn over the world. public ReadOnlySpan<MeshVertex> ViewModel { get; } Property Value ReadOnlySpan<MeshVertex> ViewModelInWorld Whether the view model is drawn with the world's projection (because the viewer's body is holding it). public bool ViewModelInWorld { get; } Property Value bool ViewModelWindow A scope's eyepiece window looked through this frame: xyz its middle in the world, w the cosine of the angle from the eye between its middle and its rim (0 for none). Looking through a scope's eyepiece (Window), the lens is that window, and the rest of the frame (the scope's body round it, the world past it) is left as drawn, as Modern Warfare's scopes are. Without one, the lens is a circle of its own and the rest of the screen is blurred and darkened. public ScopeLens(float Amount, Vector2 Offset, ScopeReticle Reticle, float Window = 0) Parameters Amount float 0 to 1, from no scope to fully up to the eye. The reticle stays on the aim point, where the shots go. The lens moves around it, and its edge shadows the side it's moving away from. public Vector2 Offset { get; init; } Property Value Vector2 Reticle The reticle drawn on the aim point. public ScopeReticle Reticle { get; init; } Property Value ScopeReticle Window The radius of the eyepiece's window on the screen, in screen heights, when looking through one; 0 for a lens drawn over the screen (Radius). public float Window { get; init; } Property Value float

api/LastFleet.Rendering.Post.ScopeReticl.summary: Enum ScopeReticle Namespace LastFleet.Rendering.Post Assembly LastFleet.Rendering.dll The reticle shown in a scope's lens (ScopeLens). Dot = 3 Just a magnified red dot, like a red dot sight seen through a magnifier.

api/LastFleet.Rendering.Rays.RayGeometry.title: Class RayGeometry | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.Rendering.Rays.RayGeometry.summary: Class RayGeometry Namespace LastFleet.Rendering.Rays Assembly LastFleet.Rendering.dll The level mesh as the rays see it: only the drawn parts (collision-only parts are left out), split into the geometries of the level's bottom-level acceleration structure. Parts that never disappear are merged into as few geometries as the mesh order allows, and are opaque, so a ray stops at them right away. Each part that can disappear (a prop that breaks, a door that opens, Gone) gets its own geometry and isn't opaque, so the shader can check every frame whether it's still there. public sealed class RayGeometry Inheritance object RayGeometry Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Properties Runs The geometries, in order. api/LastFleet.Rendering.RenderPath.html.title: Enum RenderPath | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.Rendering.RenderPath.html.summary: Enum RenderPath Namespace LastFleet.Rendering Assembly LastFleet.Rendering.dll How the renderer lights the scene. Both draw the same level, bodies, effects and HUD with the same post-processing; they differ in how light is worked out. Changing it takes effect on the next frame, with no restart. public enum RenderPath Fields Hybrid = 0 Rasterized forward shading with ray-traced shadows, bounce, occlusion and reflections where the GPU traces rays (docs/plans/ray-tracing.md), multisampled. PathTraced = 1 Path traced after NVIDIA's RTX Path Tracing (RTXPT): every pixel's light from paths through the scene, denoised by DLSS Ray Reconstruction or the built-in denoiser, and upscaled by DLSS (docs/plans/path-tracing.md). Needs a GPU that traces rays; falls back to Hybrid where there is none.

It draws the scene in HDR with multisampling (the static world mesh, flat-shaded with a depth buffer and tinted per part, plus the horde, bodies, world-space effects and the gun in hand), then applies bloom and the tone curve into the swapchain, then draws the 2D overlay and textured UI (Dear ImGui) on top. public sealed class VulkanRenderer : IDisposable Inheritance object VulkanRenderer Implements IDisposable Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Uses core Vulkan 1.3 features only: dynamic rendering (no render pass objects) and synchronization2 barriers and submits. Two frames are in flight, so the CPU records frame N+1 while the GPU draws frame N. Memory comes from VMA. Call PreloadLoader() once, before the window is created, then construct the renderer on the main thread. Constructors VulkanRenderer(GameWindow, RendererOptions) Creates the Vulkan instance, picks a GPU and builds the swapchain for window. public VulkanRenderer(GameWindow window, RendererOptions options) Parameters window GameWindow options RendererOptions Exceptions InvalidOperationException No GPU supports Vulkan 1.3 and can present to the window. Any extra are dropped. public const int MaxCaptureLights = 8192 Field Value int MaxDebrisVertices Maximum debris vertices drawn per frame: room for every fragment a DebrisWorld keeps (160, a box of 36 vertices each). Debris has this space to itself, after the dynamic world's, so a busy level never crowds it out. public const int MaxDebrisVertices = 5760 Field Value int MaxDynamicVertices Maximum dynamic world vertices (characters, loot, props, hoses) drawn per frame. Any extra are dropped, from the end of DynamicWorld (DroppedDynamicVertices). public const int MaxDynamicVertices = 196608 Field Value int MaxEffectVertices Maximum effect vertices drawn per frame. Any extra are dropped. public const int MaxEffectVertices = 12288 Field Value int MaxFogVolumes Maximum smoke volumes per frame (FogVolumes). Any extra are dropped. public const int MaxFogVolumes = 32 Field Value int MaxLights Maximum point lights per frame. Any extra are dropped, so pass the nearest first. public const int MaxLights = 128 Field Value int MaxOverlayVertices Maximum overlay vertices drawn per frame. Any extra are dropped. public const int MaxOverlayVertices = 6144 Field Value int MaxRooms Maximum number of rooms a level's RoomLighting can have. public const int MaxRooms = 512 Field Value int MaxShadows Maximum shadow maps drawn per frame. Any extra are dropped. public const int MaxShadows = 16 Field Value int MaxSkinMatrices Maximum skinned body joint matrices per frame (SkinMatrices). Bodies past that are dropped. public const int MaxSkinMatrices = 8192 Field Value int MaxSwarmInstances Maximum horde bodies drawn per frame (SetSwarmModel(AnimatedModel, ReadOnlySpan<Vector3>)). Any extra are dropped. public const int MaxSwarmInstances = 1024 Field Value int MaxViewModelVertices Maximum view model vertices (the weapon in your hands) per frame. Any extra are dropped. public const int MaxViewModelVertices = 12288 Field Value int ShadowCacheSlots Number of lights whose level shadow maps are kept from frame to frame (CacheSlot). public const int ShadowCacheSlots = 32 Field Value int Properties AmbientOcclusion How ambient occlusion is computed: off, at half resolution, or at full resolution. Changing the resolution rebuilds the frame's images before the next frame. public AmbientOcclusion AmbientOcclusion { get; set; } Property Value AmbientOcclusion Antialiasing Samples per pixel for the scene (1 is off, 2 or 4 is multisampled antialiasing). Uses the row-vector convention, like System.Numerics: clip = position * ViewProjection. GpuDetection Probes whether a dedicated (discrete) GPU is present on the host system. PngWriter Writes 8-bit RGB PNG files. Good enough for screenshots, without needing an image library. RendererOptions Renderer start-up settings. VulkanRenderer The Vulkan 1.3 renderer. It draws the scene in HDR with multisampling (the static world mesh, flat-shaded with a depth buffer and tinted per part, plus the horde, bodies, world-space effects and the gun in hand), then applies bloom and the tone curve into the swapchain, then draws the 2D overlay and textured UI (Dear ImGui) on top. Structs CameraView The camera a frame is drawn from. FrameGeometry Everything drawn on top of the static world in one frame. FrameParameters Everything the renderer needs to draw one frame. Enums RenderPath How the renderer lights the scene. Both draw the same level, bodies, effects and HUD with the same post-processing; they differ in how light is worked out. Changing it takes effect on the next frame, with no restart.

api/LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Arms.title: Enum FireMode | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Arms.summary: Enum FireMode Namespace LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Arms Assembly LastFleet.Simulation.dll How the trigger turns into shots. A gun's comes from its trigger group (see FireModeSet). public enum FireMode : byte Fields Automatic = 0 Fires for as long as the trigger is held. SemiAutomatic = 1 One shot per trigger press. Burst = 2 A fixed burst per trigger press. Manual = 3 One shot per trigger press, then the action is worked by hand (a pump or a bolt) before the next: the time between shots is the hands racking it.

api/LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Arms.summary: Enum WeaponTraits Namespace LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Arms Assembly LastFleet.Simulation.dll What a weapon does beyond its numbers (see the design doc, "Manufacturers" and "Rarity and affixes"). A trait can be a manufacturer's signature, or the effect of an affix or a relic. The numbers live in WeaponTraitRules. [Flags] public enum WeaponTraits : uint Fields None = 0 SteadyHand = 1 Kessler: more damage while crouched. Restoration = 2 Halcyon: a kill heals, and health starts regenerating right away. Scrapwork = 4 Rustline: every so often a round jams, and clearing it takes a moment. Corrosive = 8 Vashti: hits keep damaging the target over a few seconds. Arc = 16 Vashti: hits arc to the nearest other enemy. Hunger = 32 Choir-forged: each kill makes it hit harder for a while, and every shot costs a little health. Vigil = 64 More damage while holding the objective during the hack. Tolling = 128 A precision kill puts rounds back in the magazine. Lifesteal = 256 Hits heal the shooter by a fraction of the damage dealt. Suppressed = 512 A suppressor. Soldiers and the horde only hear its shots in the room they're fired in. Laser = 1024 A laser sight. Hipfire is tighter, and the beam and dot are drawn.

api/LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Arms.title: Namespace LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Arms | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Arms.summary: Namespace LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Arms Structs AmmoDrop Marks a character that drops ammo where it dies. AmmoPickup Ammo lying in the world. Walking over it tops up every carried weapon's reserve by Magazines magazines' worth. A crate (RespawnSeconds above zero) respawns after a while. A drop disappears when it's taken or when LifetimeLeft runs out. FireModeSet A set of FireModes: the ones a frame allows, or the ones a trigger group can be switched between. Switching steps through them in FireMode's order (Automatic, SemiAutomatic, Burst, Manual), round to the first, whatever order the data lists them in. FittedParts The parts fitted to a weapon to replace the ones it rolled, one per part slot (barrel, magazine, stock, optic, module, muzzle, grip, trigger, in that order). An empty slot keeps the rolled part. This is part of a WeaponIdentity, so a weapon a player has modified still only takes a few bytes to send. Grenade A live grenade, in flight or resting (or a placed device), counting down to its explosion. GrenadeBag A character's grenades: how many it carries, and how they recharge. Loadout The weapons a player carries: two of them (a main weapon and a sidearm, or any two), with one in hand. Everything else they carry is in their Inventory. PartFit One weapon part as data: which part it is (the hash of its id in the loot data, see LastFleet.Loot) and how well its ranges rolled (0 is the worst of each range, 255 the best). A Part of zero means no part. StatChange A timed stat change from using a ChangeStatAction: which stat, by how much, and how many seconds are left. StatChangeSlots The stat changes a player has active (PlayerEffects). It's an inline array so the component stays a value type. WeaponDrop A weapon lying in the world with its ammo. It can come from a loot cache, a soldier's body, or a player who swapped it for another one. A player picks it up by holding Interact next to it (see WeaponPickupSystem). WeaponFrame The kind of gun, called its frame (for example an auto rifle or a shotgun), stored as its index in the frames in play (All, the loot data's archetypes in order). It's stored and sent as that index, so the host and clients must be using the same frames. The first frame is the default. WeaponIdentity Which loot roll a weapon came from: the seed, loot table and item level it's rebuilt from. That way a weapon only takes a few bytes to send, and the HUD can name it. Table is zero for a stock (unrolled) weapon. WeaponSlot A carried weapon that isn't in hand: its stats, plus its ammo and shot counter as they were when it was put away. WeaponSlots The slots of a Loadout. WeaponState Live state of an equipped weapon. WeaponStats Physical weapon values the simulation uses. WeaponStatsResolver produces them from the designer-facing 0–100 stats, so edit the profile, not these numbers. Enums FireMode How the trigger turns into shots. A gun's comes from its trigger group (see FireModeSet). WeaponTraits What a weapon does beyond its numbers (see the design doc, "Manufacturers" and "Rarity and affixes"). A trait can be a manufacturer's signature, or the effect of an affix or a relic. The numbers live in WeaponTraitRules.

api/LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Carg.summary: Enum TankPhase Namespace LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Cargo Assembly LastFleet.Simulation.dll How far along a SupplyTank is in being emptied into the docked dropship. public enum TankPhase : byte Fields Full = 0 Untouched. The hose is on its valve, ready to be taken (hold Interact). Dragging = 1 A player is dragging the hose's end back toward the dropship. Dropped = 2 The hose's end lies where it was put down (or dropped). Anyone can pick it up again. Pumping = 3 Coupled to the dropship's port and pumping into it. The hose is there for the enemy to cut. Cut = 4 The enemy cut the hose. No pumping until a player mends it (hold Interact at the cut). Empty = 5 Fully emptied into the dropship. CastOff = 6 The dropship cast off (the hack began) before the tank was emptied. Whatever is left stays behind. Sealed = 7 A deep reservoir's outlet whose pipe still has valves shut. There's nothing to take until every valve is opened (hold Interact at each one). Then it becomes Full.

api/LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Char.summary: Struct PlayerCommand Namespace LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Characters Assembly LastFleet.Simulation.dll One tick of player intent. This is the only way input reaches the simulation. public struct PlayerCommand : IComponent Implements IComponent Inherited Members ValueType.Equals(object) ValueType.GetHashCode() ValueType.ToString() object.Equals(object, object) object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) Remarks In co-op, clients send these to the host and the host applies them on the matching tick, so the same type carries local input now and networked input later. The client writes a fresh command before each tick. Buttons are sent as held state, not presses. The simulation works out presses itself, so a lost or repeated packet can't fire a semi-automatic weapon twice. X adds to yaw (positive turns left), Y adds to pitch (positive looks up). public Vector2 Look Field Value Vector2 Move Movement axes: X is strafe right, Y is forward. Length is clamped to 1, so analog sticks give partial speed. public Vector2 Move Field Value Vector2 Op An inventory action (Inventory). Together with OpA, OpB and OpSerial, it holds the op, its slots, and a serial that changes with each new op. A client sends the same op and serial for a few ticks to make sure it arrives, and the host applies each serial only once. public InventoryOp Op Field Value InventoryOp OpA public byte OpA Field Value byte OpB public byte OpB Field Value byte OpSerial public byte OpSerial Field Value byte WeaponSlot The weapon slot wanted in hand, 1 to Capacity, or 0 for no change. api/LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Gear.title: Namespace LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Gear | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Gear.summary: Namespace LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Gear Classes ItemDefinition What an item is like (content/defs/loot/items.json): its name, model and colors, how many stack in a slot, what it's for (Roles), and the fields that its roles turn on. Items The items currently in play (ItemDefinition). Once the loot data's items.json is put in play with Use(IReadOnlyList<ItemDefinition>?), those are used. Otherwise it's the shipped ones (Shipped), which match the repository's data. In play, an item is identified by its position in the list (ItemKind). What a consumable does is defined by its effect (EffectRegistry). Structs Container A container to search, like a footlocker or a case, with its WorldPosition at the middle of its base. A player opens it by holding Interact, the same as picking up an item (see WeaponPickupSystem), and its contents are laid out on top as items to take. Once opened, it stays open. ContainerItems What's inside a Container. Inventory What a player carries besides their weapons (Loadout). There are four quick slots for consumables used in the field (medkits, ammo packs) and a pack of twelve slots for everything else, except items carried in both arms. Slots are numbered with the quick slots first (0 to 3), then the pack (4 to 15). ItemDrop Items lying in the world at their WorldPosition, resting on whatever is under them (a floor, a shelf). A player holding Interact next to them picks up whatever fits (see WeaponPickupSystem). ItemKind Identifies an item (other than weapons, which are carried in the Loadout) by its position in the items in play (Items, from the loot data's items.json), counting from 1. 0 means none. ItemPile A stack of one kind of item, either in an inventory slot or lying in the world. LootDrop Marks a character that may drop a weapon where it dies. The loot system only rolls for it once (Rolled). PackSlots The pack slots of an Inventory. QuickSlots The quick slots of an Inventory, for consumables used in the field. Enums ContainerKind What kind of Container it is. The numeric values are sent over the network, so add new ones at the end. InventoryOp Something a player does with their inventory, carried in a PlayerCommand. ItemRoles What an item is for (its flags in items.json). Each flag turns on the item fields and rules that go with it.

api/LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Miss.title: Enum ObjectiveKind | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Miss.summary: Enum ObjectiveKind Namespace LastFleet.Simulation.Components.Missions Assembly LastFleet.Simulation.dll What a mission's squad comes for (docs/plans/structure-first.md, "Objective kinds"). public enum ObjectiveKind : byte Fields Hack = 0 Hold the terminal's room while the hack runs; it opens the way to the last zone. Data = 1 Hold the terminal's room while the data comes down, then carry the drive out like a keycard: whoever has it, lost where they go down. The squad has to get off with it. Destruct = 2 Arm the self-destruct, then get off before the countdown runs out: the station locked down, its compartments sealing as it runs. Boarding = 3 A boarding action: a warship in a fight with the fleet. Silence its gun batteries and cut its power at the reactor, then take its bridge (hold it, as a hack); then get off as it dies, its compartments sealing as a self-destruct's do. While its guns fire, the fleet takes damage.

It can check whether using the effect now would do anything, and it applies the effect's actions in order. Anything that needs the world (like dropping a pod) is handed back for the caller to do. FlashAction A burst of light at the player's position. Its color is Color (each channel 0 to 1) times Brightness, it reaches Radius meters, and it fades over Seconds. It's purely visual. GiveArmorAction Gives Amount armor, up to Max. If the player already has more than Max, nothing is taken away. Armor absorbs damage after the shield and before health, and it doesn't regenerate. HealAction Heals Amount health, up to max health ("do": "heal"). PlaceDeviceAction Places a device in front of the player, on the wall ahead or on the floor. This is the breaching charge. RefillAmmoAction Adds Magazines magazines' worth of ammo to every weapon's reserve ("do": "refillAmmo"). ShieldAction A shield of Amount that absorbs damage first. It regenerates at PerSecond after DelaySeconds without taking damage. SoundAction Plays the sound Cue (a cue in content/defs/sounds.json) at the player's position, for everyone nearby. Structs EffectCueRecord A sound or flash an effect made (SoundAction, FlashAction), for the presentation to play. It records when and where, and which action of which effect. The effect is its index in EffectRegistry, which is the same on host and clients. EffectRequest Something an effect needs done in the world, which the caller of Apply(EffectDefinition, Entity, ref Loadout, in WeaponStats, ref WeaponState, ICollection<EffectRequest>) handles: dropping a pod or a device, or playing a sound or a flash. Index is the action's index in the effect's action list. Enums EffectTrigger When an effect happens (the "trigger" field in effects.json). PlayerStat The stats a stat change (ChangeStatAction) can modify. Each is changed by a fraction of its value.

api/LastFleet.Simulation.Movement.Player.summary: Class PlayerController Namespace LastFleet.Simulation.Movement Assembly LastFleet.Simulation.dll The player movement model: run, sprint, crouch, slide, jump, double jump and stamina dash, in the spirit of Destiny 2 and Witchfire. One call advances one character by one tick. public static class PlayerController Inheritance object PlayerController Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Priorities, highest first: a mantle, an active dash, starting a dash, jumping, then ground or air movement. Jumps are edge-triggered, so holding Space doesn't jump again on landing. That removes bunny-hopping. In the air, input steers the horizontal velocity toward where the player is pressing, like in Destiny. That works in any direction, whether forward is held or not, at a rate set by the air acceleration. Steering never raises horizontal speed above what the character had at the start of the tick (or its run speed), so momentum only comes from slides and dashes, and turning hard away from the direction you're flying costs speed. It's a pure function of its inputs, so it's deterministic and can be tested without a world. Fields BurdenedSpeedFactor Speed multiplier for a player dragging a downed teammate. public const float BurdenedSpeedFactor = 0.4 Field Value float CarryingSpeedFactor Speed multiplier for a player carrying a cargo crate. public const float CarryingSpeedFactor = 0.7 Field Value float Methods AirSteer(Vector3, Vector3, float, float, float) Air control. So pressing forward and to one side curves the jump without slowing it, a pure strafe turns it at run speed, and pressing back brakes it. With no input, momentum is kept. api/LastFleet.Simulation.Supplies.html.title: Namespace LastFleet.Simulation.Supplies | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.Simulation.Supplies.html.summary: Namespace LastFleet.Simulation.Supplies Classes FlatUse A fixed amount used every jump ("per": "jump"). FleetSupplies The fleet supplies currently in play (SupplyDefinition). Once the loot data's supplies.json is put in play with Use(IReadOnlyList<SupplyDefinition>?), those are used. Otherwise it's the shipped ones (Shipped), which match the repository's data. InContactUse Used only while the Scourge is on the fleet ("per": "contact"). It's what fighting the Scourge off costs. MessageShortage Writes Text to the jump's log. MoraleBonus Raises morale by Amount. If Ship names a ship kind, it only applies while a ship of that kind is still flying. MoraleShortage Lowers morale by Amount, plus one more for every PerUnits units short. A PerUnits of 0 means there's no extra drop. PeopleLostShortage Kills PerUnit people for each unit short, taken from the transports first. The log names Cause as the cause, for example "hunger" gives "40 people died of hunger.". PerDamagedShipUse Used for each ship that's still flying but damaged ("per": "damagedShip"). It's what repairs cost. PerPeopleUse Used for each People people aboard ("per": "people"). If RoundUp is true, a partial group counts as a whole one (at one per 160 people, 161 people use two); otherwise it's dropped. PerShipUse Used for each ship that's still flying ("per": "ship"). ProduceBonus Adds Amount of the item Item to the stores, like a farm's harvest. If Ship names a ship kind, it only applies while a ship of that kind is still flying. RepairShipsBonus Repairs every damaged ship by Amount condition, capped at full condition. ShipWornShortage One ship (never the flagship) loses PerUnit condition for each unit short. Message is logged, with the ship's name filled in for "{ship}". ShortageEffect Something that happens when the fleet runs short of a supply on a jump (the "short" list in supplies.json). It scales with how many units short the fleet is. Effects apply in order. StockedEffect Something that happens when the fleet has enough of a supply on a jump (the "stocked" list in supplies.json). Effects apply in order. SupplyDefinition How the fleet uses one of its supplies (content/defs/loot/supplies.json). It covers how much a jump costs (Use, with the parts added together), what happens when the fleet runs short (Shortage), what happens when it has enough (Stocked), and where the supply can be found. SupplyUse One part of how much of a supply a jump costs the fleet (the "use" list in supplies.json). All the parts are added together. Each one is a whole number of units. WhileShipUse Used while a ship of the kind Ship is still flying ("per": "shipAlive"). It's what that ship needs to keep working.

api/LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.Charact.summary: Class CharacterBodySystem Namespace LastFleet.Simulation.Systems Assembly LastFleet.Simulation.dll Moves characters through the level: velocity in, position, collision-adjusted velocity and ground contact out. Also swaps the standing and crouching capsules, keeps a character crouched where it has no room to stand, and keeps characters from walking through each other. public sealed class CharacterBodySystem : ISimulationSystem Inheritance object CharacterBodySystem Implements ISimulationSystem Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Characters block each other here in the simulation, not in Jolt. Before moving, each character loses the part of its velocity that heads into another character's capsule, and overlapping characters are eased apart. Everyone uses positions from the start of the tick, so the result doesn't depend on update order. Each looks only at the bodies in its own square of a grid and the eight around it (squares as wide as two capsules, so nobody it could touch is further), in the order the bodies were gathered: the same result as looking at every one, for a few each. api/LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.CoverSy.summary: Class CoverSystem Namespace LastFleet.Simulation.Systems Assembly LastFleet.Simulation.dll Red Orchestra style cover for soldiers, and low cover and leaning for players. A character takes low cover automatically when it faces something close by. public sealed class CoverSystem : ISimulationSystem Inheritance object CoverSystem Implements ISimulationSystem Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Crouched behind low cover (LowMin to LowMax tall), it ducks below the top, and aiming peeks just over it. Moving away from where it took cover leaves cover. A player leans out to either side anywhere with LeanLeft and LeanRight (Q and E): the eye, the shots and the head move up to LeanDistance to the side, less where a wall is in the way, and the body stays where it is. A player is never slowed by cover and never blind fires. A soldier facing a wall with an edge beside it stands behind the wall, and aiming leans it out around the edge. Firing without aiming is blind fire: the gun goes over or around the cover, the body stays hidden, and the shots are wild. While peeking a soldier moves slowly. Runs after movement and mantles (it overrides the eye height they set) and before weapons (which fire from the eye position it leaves). It looks for cover with a few rays every CheckTicks ticks per character, spread out over the ticks, and never while peeking (the cover is kept until the peek ends). It's deterministic, so the client predicts its own cover. Constructors CoverSystem(ICollisionWorld) Red Orchestra style cover for soldiers, and low cover and leaning for players. api/LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.EffectS.title: Class EffectSystem | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.EffectS.summary: Class EffectSystem Namespace LastFleet.Simulation.Systems Assembly LastFleet.Simulation.dll Applies effects to players over time (PlayerEffects). public sealed class EffectSystem : ISimulationSystem Inheritance object EffectSystem Implements ISimulationSystem Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Timed stat changes count down and expire. The passive effects of the items each player holds (Passive, counted once per item kind) are added to the running changes, and the totals are written where the game reads them (SpeedChange, DamageTakenChange, ReloadSpeedChange). The shield is whichever is stronger out of the used one and the held ones, and it regenerates after its delay without damage. Going down clears everything: stat changes, shield and armor. Runs after the life system (which tracks time since damage) and before movement, so a change applies on the same tick it's made. Only the host runs it; each client gets its own player's result in every snapshot. Doesn't allocate. Methods Held(in Inventory) Adds up the passive effects of the items in inventory, counting each item kind once. public static HeldEffects Held(in Inventory inventory) Parameters inventory Inventory Returns HeldEffects Initialize(EntityStore) Called once when the system joins a world. api/LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.LagComp.summary: Class LagCompensation Namespace LastFleet.Simulation.Systems Assembly LastFleet.Simulation.dll Lag compensation for co-op: remembers where every character was at the end of each recent tick, so a client's shot is tested against the characters where that client saw them, not where they have moved since. public sealed class LagCompensation : ISimulationSystem Inheritance object LagCompensation Implements ISimulationSystem Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks A client draws others InterpolationTicks behind the newest snapshot, and its command reaches the host later still. The host sets each client's view tick (SetViewTick(int, double)) when it applies that client's command, and ShotResolutionSystem calls TryRewind(int, int, out Vector3, out MovementState) for each character a shot might hit. Add this system last, so it records where everyone ended up at the end of the tick. Rewinding is capped at MaxRewindTicks, so a client with a worse connection than that has to lead its targets. api/LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.LifeSys.summary: Class LifeSystem Namespace LastFleet.Simulation.Systems Assembly LastFleet.Simulation.dll Handles health over time: regeneration, being downed, death and respawn. A dead character's input is ignored and its collision body is removed, so others can walk through the corpse. Players with a SpawnPoint respawn after RespawnSeconds with the stock kit (DefaultLoadout(ulong)). The weapons they found and everything in their inventory are left where they died, for them or a teammate to pick up. Soldiers stay dead. public sealed class LifeSystem : ISimulationSystem Inheritance object LifeSystem Implements ISimulationSystem Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks A player (with Rescue) who hits zero health while a teammate is still up gets downed instead. They bleed out over BleedOutSeconds, can only look, fire a sidearm, reload and ping (DownedCommand(in PlayerCommand, in Loadout)), and only die if nobody revives them in time (RescueSystem). A player on their own dies right away, as before. Runs first among the gameplay systems, but after any system that writes commands (the AI), so it can cancel them. api/LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.ShotRes.summary: Class ShotResolutionSystem Namespace LastFleet.Simulation.Systems Assembly LastFleet.Simulation.dll Resolves hitscan shots. Casts each of this tick's shots against the level and every living character, applies damage to whatever target or character it hits (including falloff and precision), and records the result in the HitLog. public sealed class ShotResolutionSystem : ISimulationSystem Inheritance object ShotResolutionSystem Implements ISimulationSystem Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Characters are hit through HitVolumes (a body capsule and a head sphere), tested with exact math, never through the physics engine. A shot stops at the first thing it hits. A character on the shooter's own side stops it without taking damage. A round is one hit: health drops pellet by pellet, but the flinch, the stagger and the push (ImpactRules) come once a round for each body it hit, from all its pellets on that body added up. Runs right after the weapon system, so shots start from where the shooter stood when firing. With lagCompensation, a co-op client's shots hit other characters where that client saw them. api/LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.html.title: Namespace LastFleet.Simulation.Systems | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.Simulation.Systems.html.summary: Namespace LastFleet.Simulation.Systems Classes CargoSystem Handles cargo crates carried in both hands (Carried, picked up by the weapon pickup system). While carrying, the player is slower, can't sprint or dash, has the weapon lowered, and can't use anything else. CharacterBodySystem Moves characters through the level: velocity in, position, collision-adjusted velocity and ground contact out. Also swaps the standing and crouching capsules, keeps a character crouched where it has no room to stand, and keeps characters from walking through each other. CharacterControllerSystem Applies each character's PlayerCommand: look first, then the movement model. CoverSystem Red Orchestra style cover for soldiers, and low cover and leaning for players. A character takes low cover automatically when it faces something close by. DestructionSystem Handles breakable props. Shots (ShotResolutionSystem) and grenades (GrenadeSystem) damage them through this system. When a prop breaks, its collision is switched off so it stops blocking movement, sight and shots, and the break is recorded in the DestructionLog. DropFallSystem Makes loot fall when whatever it was resting on breaks (docs/plans/furniture.md). Every weapon, pile, case and cargo crate resting on a prop that broke this tick (inside its bounds, from its base to a little above its top) starts falling, and keeps falling under gravity until a ray finds something to land on. Positions go out in snapshots as normal, so clients see it fall. EffectSystem Applies effects to players over time (PlayerEffects). GrenadeSystem Frag grenades. Handles throwing them (a fresh press of Grenade throws along the view), flying and bouncing off the level, and exploding when the fuse runs out. Explosions damage the thrower's enemies if there's a clear line from the blast, with damage falling off with distance, and are recorded in the ExplosionLog. HullPulls How an open breach (HullPull) drags whoever can see it: like a wind, a drift added to where they move each tick (CharacterBodySystem), so ground friction doesn't eat it and running away still counts. It's strongest at the breach, falling off evenly to nothing at its reach, only in front of the wall it's in and only in sight of it. The same on the host and in a client's prediction, which runs the same body step. Interaction Works out what a player is looking at, for interacting with it. A thing counts as looked at when the line of sight from the eye passes within its radius (treating it as an upright column from its base up to its height) and it's close enough to reach. InventorySystem Applies the inventory actions (InventoryOp) players send in their commands to their Inventory. LagCompensation Lag compensation for co-op: remembers where every character was at the end of each recent tick, so a client's shot is tested against the characters where that client saw them, not where they have moved since. LifeSystem Handles health over time: regeneration, being downed, death and respawn. A dead character's input is ignored and its collision body is removed, so others can walk through the corpse. Players with a SpawnPoint respawn after RespawnSeconds with the stock kit (DefaultLoadout(ulong)). The weapons they found and everything in their inventory are left where they died, for them or a teammate to pick up. Soldiers stay dead. LoadoutSystem Switches weapons. When a command asks for another slot, the weapon in hand is stowed in its slot and the new one is brought up, and it can't fire until its swap time has passed. A reload in progress is lost, like in Destiny. MantleSystem Starts and drives mantles. Runs after the controller, so it can take over this tick's velocity. PickupSystem Ammo pickups in the world. Characters with an AmmoDrop leave a pickup where they die, and players who walk over a pickup take it if any of their weapons has room. Dropped pickups disappear after a while; crates respawn. PingSystem Pings. Pressing Ping marks whatever is in the middle of the player's view: an enemy there (with a little leeway, so it doesn't need perfect aim), or otherwise the spot where the view hits the level. RescueSystem Reviving and dragging downed teammates (design doc, "Downed, revive and drag"). ShotResolutionSystem Resolves hitscan shots. Casts each of this tick's shots against the level and every living character, applies damage to whatever target or character it hits (including falloff and precision), and records the result in the HitLog. TankSystem Handles dragging supply tank hoses (SupplyTank). TargetSystem Stands destroyed targets back up, at full health, once their respawn time has passed. WeaponPickupSystem Handles everything a player uses with Interact: weapons and items in the world, containers, cargo, pods, supply tanks and the dropship's hold. Most take a press; searching a container and turning a valve take a hold. WeaponSystem Runs the weapon model for every armed character and records shots in the ShotLog. WeaponTraitSystem Applies weapon trait effects (WeaponTraits) after this tick's shots are resolved. Structs HeldEffects The combined passive effects of everything a player is holding (see Held(in Inventory)). Interfaces IShownCharacters Where each client was shown the other characters. In co-op the host knows this from what it sent each client. IShownHorde Where each client was shown the horde. In co-op the host knows this from what it sent each client. A client's shots at swarmlings are resolved against these positions, so it hits what it saw (see LagCompensation). Enums PodUse The result of holding Interact at a cargo pod (see LoadOrCall(ref CargoPod, ref Inventory)).

api/LastFleet.Simulation.Weapons.WeaponS.summary: Class WeaponStatsResolver Namespace LastFleet.Simulation.Weapons Assembly LastFleet.Simulation.dll Turns a designer-facing WeaponProfile into the physical WeaponStats the simulation uses. public static class WeaponStatsResolver Inheritance object WeaponStatsResolver Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Every stat maps linearly between a worst value at 0 and a best value at 100, so players can read a roll and designers can reason about it. The curves are first-pass tuning. Fields LaserHipSpread Hip spread with a laser sight, as a fraction of the frame's normal hip spread. public const float LaserHipSpread = 0.7 Field Value float MaxRecoilAngleDegrees The largest sideways recoil angle, reached at recoil direction 0, in degrees. public const float MaxRecoilAngleDegrees = 35 Field Value float Methods RecoilAngle(int) Returns the recoil angle for a recoil direction stat. 100 kicks straight up. Lower values lean further sideways: even values to the right, odd values to the left, so two rolls with the same points can still feel different. public static float RecoilAngle(int recoilDirection) Parameters recoilDirection int Returns float Resolve(in WeaponProfile) Resolves a profile into stats. Stats outside 0–100 are clamped. The magazine always keeps at least one round and the zoom is at least 1×. public static WeaponStats Resolve(in WeaponProfile profile) Parameters profile WeaponProfile Returns WeaponStats

api/LastFleet.Simulation.Weapons.html.title: Namespace LastFleet.Simulation.Weapons | The Last Fleet
api/LastFleet.Simulation.Weapons.html.summary: Namespace LastFleet.Simulation.Weapons Classes DestructionLog The props that broke this tick. Cleared every tick. The client uses it to hide the props and spawn debris. ExplosionLog The explosions that went off this tick. Cleared every tick, like the HitLog. The client draws them. HandActions Works out what a character's hands are doing (HandAction) from its state. It checks, in this order: using an item, throwing a grenade, reloading, and a shot just fired. This is only for drawing the body; it doesn't read or change anything the simulation depends on. HitLog What this tick's shots hit: one record per shot, in firing order. Cleared every tick, so read it after Step() returns. The client draws hit markers, impacts and tracers from it, and co-op will send it to clients. ImpactRules How a round's push (a frame's Impact) moves what it hits, read from the loot data (content/defs/loot/impact.json). Default holds the values the game ships with. Pushes are in meters a second: the speed a round gives a body, before the body's friction takes it back. ShotLog The shots fired during the current tick. Cleared at the start of each weapon update, so read it after Step() returns. Hit detection will consume it once physics exists. SoldierUse How a frame changes the way a soldier fights with it (the frame's "soldier" data). WeaponArchetype The fixed traits of a weapon frame, the things that make an auto rifle an auto rifle. The stats on a WeaponProfile scale these values. WeaponArchetypes The weapon frames. Each one is an archetype from the loot data (archetypes.json) with its model file, how it fires, its fire rate, magazine, damage, spread and so on. WeaponHandling The gunplay model, Destiny style: trigger modes and exact cadence, magazines and reloads, aim down sights, spread and bloom, and recoil that kicks the view and partly recovers. One call advances one weapon by one tick. WeaponStatsResolver Turns a designer-facing WeaponProfile into the physical WeaponStats the simulation uses. WeaponTraitRules The tuning numbers behind WeaponTraits, read from the loot data (content/defs/loot/traits.json). Default holds the values the game ships with. Each trait should be noticeable in a fight but never decide one on its own. Structs BreakRecord A prop that broke this tick. DamageProfile How much a shot hurts, and pushes, at a given distance and hit location. ExplosionRecord One explosion and what it did. HitRecord Where one shot ended and what it did. ShotRecord One fired round, ready for hit detection. TriggerGroup What a gun's trigger group (its trigger part) does to how it fires: the modes it can be switched between and the one it starts in, and its rate of fire and burst against the frame's. The default (no modes) leaves the frame's own fire mode, rate and burst, as a gun rolled before triggers were parts has. WeaponProfile A weapon as designers and the loot generator see it: an archetype plus Destiny-style 0–100 stats, and three scales on the frame's own values that weapon parts can nudge (for example a coil barrel hits harder, a drum holds more, a scope zooms further). Parts and affixes adjust these, never the raw physical values. Enums SoldierRole The squad role a frame gives the soldier carrying it, if the squad has that role to fill. WeaponFiring How a frame's rounds travel. Each value is a firing code path in the game, picked by the frame's "firing" data.
